comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 A more concrete comparison to the related work:

| model | parameters (active / total) | base-model training tokens | approximate base-training FLOPs | RL tokens / FLOPs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [MAI-Thinking-1 / MAI-Base-1](https://microsoft.ai/pdf/mai-thinking-1.pdf) | 35B / ~1T | 30T pretraining + 3.55T mid-training | 6.30e24 pretraining; 7.05e24 including mid-training | about 1.8T packed learner tokens and 3.8e23 policy-update FLOPs for the plotted STEM climb under the reconstruction below; full RL total is higher and not recoverable |
| [OLMo 3 Think 32B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13961) | 32B / 32B | 5.5T pretraining + 2×100B mid-training branches + 100B context extension | 1.06e24 pretraining; 1.11e24 including both mid-training branches and context extension | not reported; the published hyperparameters imply at most 25.2B response tokens and about 6.4e21 nominal model FLOPs for generation + one learner pass |
| [Arcee Trinity-Large-Thinking](https://www.arcee.ai/blog/trinity-large-thinking) | 13B / 398B | 17T | 1.33e24 | not reported; the final model followed two months of SFT/RL pipeline work across 1,152 H100s. Continuous use for 60 days would be about 5.9e24 peak hardware FLOPs, but this is a mixed program envelope, not reported RL spend |
| [Kimi K2 (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534) | 32B / 1.04T | 15.5T | 2.98e24 | not reported |
| [DeepSeek V4 Pro](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19348) | 49B / 1.6T | 33T | 9.70e24 | not reported; the report describes specialist RL followed by on-policy distillation, but gives no total |

The base-training FLOPs above are my `6 × active parameters × training tokens` calculations. They are useful-model FLOPs, not measured hardware FLOPs, and they do not include ablations or failed runs. In particular, they are not directly comparable to the peak hardware-budget FLOPs in the issue without an MFU/goodput conversion.

<details>
<summary>MAI RL derivation and caveats</summary>

MAI does expose enough to estimate the learner side of its main STEM climb. The report gives a packed global batch of 7,040 sequences, a rollout-length curriculum of 8K → 16K → 32K → 64K → 128K, and a STEM curve that reaches about 5,000 steps. Reading that curve as roughly 1,000 steps at each length gives:

`7,040 × 1,000 × (8,192 + 16,384 + 32,768 + 65,536 + 131,072) = 1.788T packed learner tokens`

At 35B active parameters, that is about `3.75e23` policy-update FLOPs using `6NT`. One rollout-generation pass over the same tokens adds about `1.25e23` using `2NT`, for about `5.01e23` nominal model FLOPs across the accepted generation + learner path.

This is still not the full MAI RL bill. The paper does not tabulate the exact step boundary for each length, so the approximately 1K steps per stage is an inference from the approximately 5K-step plot. Generation also includes early-exit samples and rejected rollout groups. In addition, MAI trained separate STEM, agentic, and helpfulness/safety specialists, then ran consolidation SFT and a final RL stage. The report plots about 1.3K agentic steps, but does not expose enough trajectory-length accounting to convert those cleanly; it does not give corresponding totals for the helpfulness/safety or final consolidation climbs. The report’s largest RL job used 4,864 GB300s—4,096 for inference and 768 for the learner—but gives no duration.

One correction to the earlier discussion still stands: MAI’s 3.55T-token number is mid-training, not RL. The separate reconstruction above is why “roughly 2T RL learner tokens” is nevertheless a reasonable description of the main STEM climb.

</details>

<details>
<summary>OLMo 3 RL derivation and caveats</summary>

For OLMo 3, `750 steps × 128 prompts × 8 responses × 32,768 max response tokens = 25.2B` maximum response tokens. Applying `2NT` for rollout generation and `6NT` for one policy update gives about `6.4e21` FLOPs. That is not a reported total: real responses are usually shorter, while prompt prefill, verifiers, reference/teacher work, failed samples, and systems overhead add compute.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Arcee checkpoint distinction and hardware ceiling</summary>

The February [Trinity Large technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17004) covers Trinity-Large-Preview, not the final Trinity-Large-Thinking post-training run. Preview was instruction-tuned on [20B tokens](https://huggingface.co/arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Preview) and received a “short RL stage”; Arcee does not give its RL tokens or FLOPs.

Trinity-Large-Thinking is a separate checkpoint built from Trinity-Large-Base. Arcee’s April release report says it followed two months of work improving and scaling the SFT/RL pipeline, with post-training across 1,152 H100s. As a loose ceiling, `1,152 × 989e12 BF16 FLOP/s × 60 days = 5.91e24` peak hardware FLOPs. That period includes SFT, recipe development, experiments, and the final model run, and Arcee does not report full-cluster uptime or MFU. I therefore would not call 5.9e24 the model’s RL FLOPs or infer an RL-token count from it.

</details>

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

The Qwen3 32B-to-0.6B study is complete. A two-seed, 100 million-token screen compared five research treatments and four controls. Factorized initialization was the only research treatment promoted to a fresh 1.8 billion-token extension, but its early advantage reversed: it ended at mean NLL 2.6644, 0.39% worse than scratch forward KL at 2.6541. Official Qwen3 0.6B Base initialization plus forward KL was strongest at 2.5579 NLL and 0.3934 mean zero-shot accuracy.

Use official Base plus forward KL when checkpoint provenance is acceptable, and plain forward KL from scratch otherwise. Factorized initialization is useful only for short budgets; projected all-layer matching, TAID, weight-saliency initialization, and the 4B capacity-gap control did not justify extension.

### Helpful links
- [Results and methods report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7671/files#diff-827dbbb1efb2f80ce249ec12cbef9dafc025f6b43869b04482cfc816fdc793b8)
- [Implementation and report PR #7671](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7671)
- [W&B run group](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/groups/QD-qwen32b-to-0p6b)
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

The requested dense Qwen3.5 32B and 0.6B pair is unavailable. The experiment uses pinned Qwen3 32B, Qwen3 0.6B Base, and Qwen3 4B checkpoints, preserving the requested compression ratio but not claiming Qwen3.5 results.

## Protocol

The screen stops after 100,007,936 tokens. The extension stops after 1,800,011,776 tokens. Both use two paired seeds, sequence length 2,048, global batch size 8, a common regional Datakit sample, terminal held-out NLL as the primary endpoint, and zero-shot ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande as a regression check.

The five research treatments are projected per-layer activation distillation, rank-512 factorized initialization, TAID, teacher weight-saliency initialization, and a 4B capacity-gap control. Scratch and official-Base hard-label and forward-KL runs provide four controls.

## Result

Factorized initialization improved mean NLL over scratch KL by 1.47% at 450 million tokens, but finished 0.39% worse at 1.8 billion tokens with both paired seeds worse. Official Base plus KL finished 3.63% better than scratch KL and had the highest mean accuracy on every zero-shot task. Exact online 32B KL ran at about 28,000 tokens/s versus 95,000–97,000 tokens/s for hard-label training.

All ten terminal extension checkpoints restored and evaluated successfully. This includes the four hard-label retries that crossed the former step-10,000 Hugging Face export failure boundary. Late W&B and controller cleanup failures did not affect terminal artifacts; missing metrics were recovered from durable finelog records.

## Conclusion

Use official Base plus forward KL when possible. If training must start from scratch, use ordinary forward KL. Do not carry factorized initialization into a long run based only on a short screen; its benefit was transient in this study.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Scope:** research/experiment scaffold, not a bug — no PR. Analysis for a human to review before implementation begins.

# Research

Distillation infrastructure does not exist in Levanter yet. `models/loss.py` has only next-token CE (+ logsumexp/z-loss); there is no KL/soft-target/temperature loss and no teacher forward pass in the training step. The trainer takes a single `ComputeLossFunction` closure, so a distillation loss is pluggable, but a second (teacher) model must be threaded into the step, kept detached, mp-cast, and sharded. Weight loading from HF (both 32B teacher and 0.6B student) is well supported; **model surgery is not** — only vocab resize exists, so methods 3 (factorized init) and 4 (depth/width structured init) need new tree-surgery utilities over the `haliax` `Stacked`/`BlockSeq` layer stacks.

Two open issues cover a *different* regime — on-policy distillation for RL post-training (#5853; RFC #7236: teacher serving, top-K sparse logprobs in an RL loop). This issue is offline logit distillation + teacher-init for pretraining a 0.6B student. Related but not overlapping; align the KL/top-K loss with #7236 so the loss code is shared, not forked.

One factual flag: the TL;DR correctly notes `Qwen3.5-32B` does not exist. Confirm exact HF repo IDs before launch — `Qwen3Config` defaults to `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and Qwen3 dense tops out at 32B, but the `-Base` suffixes in the plan should be pinned to real repos.

**Relevant code**
- [`train_lm.py#L202-L209`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/main/train_lm.py#L202-L209) — loss closure + single-model `Trainer(...)`; distillation loss plugs in here
- [`loss.py#L35-L142`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/loss.py#L35-L142) — CE/z-loss only; no KL/soft-target
- [`qwen.py#L299-L396`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/qwen.py#L299-L396) — `Qwen3Config`/`Qwen3LMHeadModel`, HF converter ready
- [`model_init.py#L24-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/main/model_init.py#L24-L93) — load pretrained HF model, sharded/dtype-cast (teacher + student)
- [`trainer.py#L260-L309`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L260-L309) — `ComputeLossFunction` injection point

# Proposed approach

Build the scaffold in three landable pieces, not one PR. Screen all five arms + the scratch control at a fixed token budget; extend finalists only after the matrix completes.

1. **Distillation loss + dual-model step.** New `models/distill_loss.py`: temperature-scaled forward-KL over teacher logits, `alpha`-blended with student CE. Thread a frozen, sharded teacher into the train step (co-located forward; detached, mp-cast). This covers arm 1 (logit distillation) and the scratch control. Keep the KL top-K compatible with #7236 so the loss is shared.

2. **Model-surgery utilities.** `eqx.tree_at`-based helpers over the `Stacked` layer stack: layer selection/slicing (depth) and width projection/factorization of embeddings and attention/MLP blocks. Covers arms 3 (factorized init) and 4 (structured depth/width init). Unit-test each transform on a tiny config against exact shape and parameter-count invariants — real, testable transforms, not wrappers.

3. **Intermediate-layer + assistant arms.** Arm 2 (projected intermediate distillation) needs a learned student→teacher hidden projection and activation capture; materializing teacher activations may dominate step time (the hypothesis already flags this — measure it). Arm 5 (teacher-assistant curriculum) is orchestration over arms 1/3 with a 4B intermediate, best expressed as an `experiments/distill/` config matrix following the `experiments/grug/base/train.py` nested-dataclass + Iris-dispatch pattern.

Open questions before code:
- Exact HF repo IDs for the 32B teacher / 4B assistant / 0.6B student (`-Base` variants).
- Shared token budget and the fixed val-loss and teacher-divergence thresholds (stopping criteria) — needed to define "done" for the screening matrix.
- Memory plan: co-locate teacher forward vs. precompute top-K soft labels offline. Does the 32B teacher fit alongside 0.6B training on `cw-us-east-08a`, or do we cache teacher logits to storage first? This gates piece 1.

spillover_issues.author: weaverbot
spillover_issues.body:
Agentic presets added in #7575 point at Hugging Face repositories containing raw Harbor task directories. The current adapter calls [`snapshot_download`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/774b1a1bbbd9bafb0cfcfdc551dd8f9519bc30f9/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor_dataset.py#L13-L44) into evaluator-local `/tmp` for each job. A two-task `tb2-lite` smoke fetched all 861 repository files. Model sweeps therefore repeat the full download, depend on Hugging Face availability and rate limits during evaluation, and record the mutable revision `main`.

Harbor cannot currently consume a cached `gs://` or `s3://` task tree directly. Its pinned [`DatasetConfig.path`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/0d0dbe8904ed984137a0dfa764583f1508cf3274/src/harbor/models/job/config.py#L28-L40) is a `pathlib.Path`; dataset discovery and [task parsing](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/0d0dbe8904ed984137a0dfa764583f1508cf3274/src/harbor/models/task/task.py#L51-L86) use local path operations. Marin can still reuse its existing revision-pinned [`download_hf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/774b1a1bbbd9bafb0cfcfdc551dd8f9519bc30f9/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/huggingface.py#L291-L380) artifact path by mirroring once into regional object storage and staging the task tree locally at the Harbor boundary.

The same cleanup should replace [`download_from_gcs` and `upload_to_gcs`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/774b1a1bbbd9bafb0cfcfdc551dd8f9519bc30f9/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/utils.py#L15-L47). These helpers construct a GCS filesystem even when Harbor receives the CoreWeave `s3://` records prefix, and their names, `print` output, and existence semantics obscure that mismatch.

Done when:

- Agentic Hugging Face repositories are pinned to immutable commits and reused as Marin data artifacts instead of being downloaded from Hugging Face by every evaluation job.
- Each evaluator uses a region-local mirror: GCS on GCP and S3 on CoreWeave. Cache selection does not silently transfer large task repositories across regions.
- A generic fsspec tree-transfer API replaces the GCS-specific evaluation helpers. It derives the filesystem from each URI, uses logging, has explicit overwrite/resume behavior, and has behavior tests covering local, GCS-shaped, and S3-shaped paths.
- Harbor trial restore and upload use the generic transfer path and work with the CoreWeave S3 records prefix.
- The Harbor adapter stages the minimum required local task tree before constructing `DatasetConfig(path=...)`; a normal cached run does not contact Hugging Face.
- Eval provenance records the Hugging Face repository, immutable commit, and resolved mirror URI.
- Native Harbor object-store input is investigated across `DatasetConfig`, task discovery and parsing, checksums, Docker/build contexts, and sandbox uploads. If direct `UPath`/fsspec support removes meaningful staging, implement or upstream it with tests. If Harbor still needs local files for build or sandbox APIs, document that boundary and keep staging in Marin.
- A capped Harbor evaluation succeeds from both a regional cache and the CoreWeave S3 result path. Repeating the evaluation demonstrates cache reuse without another Hugging Face download.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 This is a multi-module design task (>100 LOC across evaluation, datakit, the Harbor adapter, plus a possible Harbor upstream), so per the fix-issue workflow I'm posting analysis for review rather than a PR.

# Research

The Harbor evaluator downloads its task tree from Hugging Face on every job. On `main`, [`harbor_evaluator.py#L370`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/harbor_evaluator.py#L370) calls `snapshot_download(..., repo_type="dataset")` into an evaluator-local workdir cache pinned to the mutable `main` revision. The agentic presets in #7575 (still open; `harbor_dataset.py` lives on `weaver/agentic-evals-unify`, not `main`) route these HF repos through that path, so model sweeps re-download the full tree and depend on HF availability and rate limits at eval time.

The GCS helpers are also backend-hardcoded. [`evaluation/utils.py#L15-L47`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/utils.py#L15-L47) build `marin_filesystem("gcs")` unconditionally, but [`harbor_runner.py#L124-L137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor_runner.py#L124-L137) / [`#L238-L242`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor_runner.py#L238-L242) pass an `out_path` that on CoreWeave is an `s3://` records prefix — a latent backend mismatch, compounded by `print` output and existence-based skip semantics.

**Relevant code**
- [`harbor_evaluator.py#L352-L384`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/harbor_evaluator.py#L352-L384) — HF `snapshot_download` → `DatasetConfig(path=...)`
- [`utils.py#L15-L47`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/utils.py#L15-L47) — GCS-only `download_from_gcs`/`upload_to_gcs`
- [`harbor_runner.py#L124-L137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor_runner.py#L124-L137) — trial restore/upload over `out_path` (may be `s3://`)
- [`download_hf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/huggingface.py#L291) — existing revision-pinned HF→object-store mirror to reuse

# Proposed approach

Design change, split into reviewable PRs. Sequenced because the HF-artifact work sits on top of #7575.

**1. Generic fsspec tree transfer (independent of the rest).** Replace the two GCS helpers with a URI-driven pair, e.g. `transfer_tree(src_uri, dst_uri, *, overwrite, resume)`, deriving each filesystem from its URI via `url_to_fs`, logging instead of `print`, with explicit overwrite/resume. Update the four call sites in `harbor_evaluator.py` and `harbor_runner.py`. This alone fixes the `s3://` mismatch and is the smallest shippable slice. Behavior tests over local, `memory://` (GCS-shaped), and `s3://`-shaped paths — real transfers, no mocks. (Before adding a new module, confirm datakit/`rigging.filesystem` has no existing generic tree-transfer to extend — I did not find one.)

**2. Regional HF mirror as a Marin artifact.** Mirror each agentic HF repo once into region-local storage (GCS on GCP, S3 on CoreWeave) via `download_hf` pinned to an immutable commit, then stage the tree locally at the Harbor boundary using the transfer from step 1. Region selection must not cross-region-copy (AGENTS.md cost rule). Record the HF repo id, resolved commit, and mirror URI in eval provenance. Depends on #7575's `harbor_dataset.py`.

**3. Native Harbor object-store input (investigation → upstream or document).** Check whether Harbor's `DatasetConfig.path` (a `pathlib.Path`), task discovery/parsing, checksums, Docker build contexts, and sandbox uploads can consume a `UPath`/fsspec tree directly. If yes, upstream `UPath` support to `marin-community/harbor` with tests and drop the staging. If Harbor still needs local files, document that boundary and keep staging in Marin.

**Open questions before implementation**
- Materialize the regional mirror once as a standalone `download_hf` step referenced by URI, or mirror lazily on first eval per region?
- Is there an existing generic fsspec tree-transfer in datakit/`rigging` I should extend instead of adding a new module?
- Land step 1 now against `main` (it fixes the `s3://` bug independently) and stack steps 2–3 on #7575?

spillover_issues.author: yonromai
spillover_issues.body:
> **Review requested** — the full plan for publishing the Snowball checkpoint (#6811, step-42150): what ships, the complete model card, and a tested inference path. Approving the four decisions below unblocks #7366; I execute after review. cc @ClassicLarry @Helw150 @rjpower ## Critical decisions 1. **Repo id: `marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base`.** Codename-forward, self-describing size, `-base` per the `marin-8b-base` precedent. Every tested command assumes it — renaming after upload breaks them, so this is the one to bikeshed *now*. 2. **Chat template: ship or strip?** The tree bundles the shared Marin tokenizer's full chat template, but the base model has no chat training — `/v1/chat/completions` answers, then hallucinates fake `user`/`assistant` turns (transcript below), and anything calling `apply_chat_template` (fine-tuning frameworks, eval harnesses) will silently treat the model as chat-capable. **(a)** Ship + card warning: keeps the weight tree untouched, helps humans but not programmatic consumers. **(b)** Strip the template[^strip]: correct capability signaling; costs a re-cut + re-pin + smoke re-test, but *not* new parity numerics — the parity suite feeds explicit token IDs and never uses the template. External review leans (b); weights are identical either way. 3. **No private staging: upload public → verify → announce.** The free-org private-storage cap is 100 GB, under the 125 GiB tree[^storage]. Public storage is free, and the artifact risk is retired pre-upload (hash-pinned, parity-tested, live-tested below). To be candid: the repo is publicly discoverable (org page, feeds) from the moment upload starts, and deletion is a failure response, not a recall — accepted because the artifact is verified before upload begins. 4. **License & data disclosure.** Proposal: `apache-2.0` (marin-8b precedent) — but precedent isn't approval; a release owner should explicitly approve the license for *these weights*, and we ship a `LICENSE` file (plus `NOTICE` if required) alongside the README. The team also needs to supply a one-paragraph training-data description covering the full 2.3T-token lineage (the card currently describes only the 211B cooldown mix) and state decontamination status. [^strip]: Stripping must cover both `chat_template.jinja` and any `chat_template` field embedded in `tokenizer_config.json`. [^storage]: [HF storage limits](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/storage-limits): free org = 100 GB private, public = free; PRO ($9/mo) = 1 TB private. marin-community shows no paid-plan badge, but only an org admin can confirm billing — preflight item below. CoreWeave egress = $0. If the org turns out to have paid private storage, staging privately first is a strictly-nicer variant of the same plan. ## What ships The pinned bf16 export tree `d819cbc63780bd86` — re-cut by #7458 under the single-name config contract (#7447); exactly reproduced from the checkpoint, with Levanter parity and the 64-case vLLM representative set matching the frozen goldens — plus `README.md` and `LICENSE`, which sit outside the hashed tree. | Asset | Details | |---|---| | Weights | 39 safetensors shards, bf16, ~125 GiB; 44-file core-tree digest `tree-sha256 = d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded) | | `config.json` | Single-name contract (#7447 Option A) — verified in the shipped file: one key per field, no aliases | | Tokenizer | `tokenizer.json` (17 MB) + `tokenizer_config.json` — Marin tokenizer, 128,256 vocab | | `chat_template.jinja` | Decision 2 | | `model.safetensors.index.json` | Shard index | | `README.md`, `LICENSE` | Added at upload (outside the hashed tree) | Not shipped: optimizer states / raw Levanter checkpoint (stay internal), `generation_config.json` (absent from the export; vLLM reads EOS/BOS from `config.json`). ## Release steps - [x] Config contract merged, export re-cut (#7447 → #7458; only `config.json` changed, weights byte-identical) - [x] Fork tag **`snowball-v1`** created — a curated pointer the card commands reference; currently at `afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14` (what `marin.inference.tpu_vllm_pins` pins for serving), advancing as the fork improves. The exact tested revision is recorded in the card's Provenance - [x] Card commands tested end-to-end on 8×H100 (protocol below) - [ ] Team review of this issue (decisions 1–4) + training-data paragraph from decision 4 - [ ] Preflight: name the uploader; org admin confirms billing plan and repo create/write/delete permissions; HF write token on the upload node (never echoed to logs) - [ ] Create public repo, `hf upload-large-folder` the tree from a CoreWeave node, add README + LICENSE - [ ] **Verification gate** (all pass/fail, before any announcement): (1) on a clean HF cache *without credentials*, download the repo; (2) verify the exact 44-file list and core-tree digest, bf16-only tensors, and single-name config; (3) serve the downloaded snapshot with the card command on 8×H100-80GB and reproduce the greedy completion; (4) rerun the 64 representative vLLM parity cases against it; (5) check rendered card, links, and license files. Card fixes happen now, not after. - [ ] Capture the final Hub commit SHA, create a Hub tag (`step-42150`), and record both plus the tested fork SHA in the card's Provenance — announce that revision, not moving `main` - [ ] Announce; housekeeping: close #7447 + #7366, delete the old `781bc329` tree (per #7458), add to the Hero Runs collection Failure response: public availability begins when upload starts; if the gate fails, stop, delete or repair the repo, and assume already-downloaded bytes cannot be recalled. After announcing, released revisions are preserved and fixes land as new commits. ## Model card (full `README.md`)
README.md as it will appear on the Hub ````markdown --- license: apache-2.0 language: - en pipeline_tag: text-generation library_name: vllm tags: - moe - mixture-of-experts - base-model - marin - grug --- # Snowball — Grug 67B-A2B base checkpoint (2.3T training tokens) **Snowball** is a research checkpoint from the [Marin project](https://marin.community): a 67B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model with ~2B active non-embedding parameters per token (Marin's **Grug** architecture), released as a **base model**. It is an *early* checkpoint — an intermediate cooldown taken ~2.3T tokens into a planned 10T-token run — not a final release. > ⚠️ **Stock `transformers`, `vllm`, and `sglang` cannot load this model.** The > architecture (`model_type: grug_moe`) is deliberately not upstreamed yet — it is still > evolving. Use [Marin's vLLM fork](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) pinned below; > it registers the architecture natively (no `trust_remote_code`). The 8×H100 vLLM > command below is the supported external path; other links are reference implementations. ## Model Sources - **Project page:** [marin.community](https://marin.community) - **Core repo:** [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin) - **Model definition (JAX/Levanter):** [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/grug/moe/model.py) · [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py) - **Training config (this checkpoint's cooldown):** [`moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py) - **Inference:** [marin-community/vllm](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) (GPU — supported path) · [marin-community/tpu-inference](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference) (TPU — reference) - **Training run:** [marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811) · [W&B logs](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k) ## Quickstart (vLLM fork, 8×H100-80GB) Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a recent NVIDIA driver — no CUDA toolkit needed with the flags below. ```sh VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ uvx --from 'vllm @ git+https://github.com/marin-community/vllm.git@snowball-v1' \ vllm serve marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN ``` `snowball-v1` is a curated tag that advances as the fork improves; the exact revision this card was verified against is in [Provenance](#provenance). On the tested node, first launch took ~10 min after weights were local (~4 min one-time `uvx` setup + ~6 min server startup); warm starts ~6 min. The 125 GiB download depends on your network. ```sh curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}' ``` Why these flags: 5 KV heads don't divide across 8 GPUs, so the model runs tensor-parallel 1 with its 256 experts sharded across GPUs (~17 GB/GPU). `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` uses prebuilt kernels instead of compiling the fork; `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` selects the parity-validated backend; the sampler env var avoids a FlashInfer path that JIT-compiles with `nvcc` at startup. ## Architecture | | | |---|---| | Total / active parameters | 67B / ~2B non-embedding active per token | | Hidden size | 2560 | | Layers | 26 — full-attention (NoPE) on every 4th + the last; 2,048-token sliding window (half-RoPE) elsewhere | | Attention | 20 heads / 5 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128, attention temperature `qk_mult ≈ 1.5703` | | Experts | 256 routed, 4 active per token, expert FFN 1280, shared expert FFN 2560 | | Context | 65,536 positions (served here at 32,768) | | Vocabulary | 128,256 (Marin tokenizer) | Grug combines QB load-balanced sigmoid expert routing, GatedNorm, exclusive self-attention (XSA), and the hybrid sliding/full attention split — which is why stock inference stacks cannot load it. Reference implementations: the pinned vLLM fork and Levanter's `SnowballConfig`. ## Training Snowball was produced by branching at step 39,000 (≈ **2.11T tokens**, ~21% of schedule) of Marin's in-progress 10T-token run ([marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811)) and applying a completed **211B-token** early cooldown (3,150 steps): Datakit phase-1 mix, sequence length switched 8,192 → 65,536, Muon learning rate decayed to the schedule floor, on TPU v4-2048. The checkpoint is complete; the parent 10T run and post-trained variants are outside this release. ## Evaluation Selected comparisons from Marin's six-model eval run ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345) — full grid and protocol there). HumanEval used the completions API for every model. | | mmlu | arc-c | hellaswag | winogrande | truthfulqa | boolq | piqa | obqa | gsm8k | humaneval | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | snowball | 0.692 | 0.642 | 0.831 | 0.714 | 0.460 | 0.833 | 0.832 | 0.474 | 0.738 | 0.598 | | qwen3-8b | 0.749 | 0.675 | 0.765 | 0.704 | 0.544 | 0.866 | 0.774 | 0.416 | 0.897 | 0.628 | | llama3.1-8b-instruct | 0.664 | 0.608 | 0.802 | 0.739 | 0.545 | 0.855 | 0.814 | 0.462 | 0.801 | 0.622 | Metrics: acc (mmlu 5-shot, winogrande, boolq); acc_norm (arc-c 25-shot, hellaswag 10-shot, piqa, obqa); mc2 (truthfulqa); exact_match flexible-extract (gsm8k 5-shot); pass@1 (humaneval). ## Limitations - **Base model.** No instruction tuning, no RLHF, no safety training. It continues text; it does not follow instructions or chat. It has not been safety-evaluated and may generate inaccurate, biased, or harmful text; not intended for high-stakes use. - **The bundled chat template is not trained behavior.** It comes from the shared Marin tokenizer. `/v1/chat/completions` will respond, but expect hallucinated extra conversation turns. Use the completions API. - **Weak long-prompt performance.** 7 of 26 layers attend beyond the 2,048-token window, but performance degrades with prompt length; some long-prompt MMLU subjects score near chance ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345)). - English-centric training mix. ## Provenance - Checkpoint: step 42,150 of run `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k-79ebf3` - Export: bf16, 44-file core-tree sha256 `d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded), reproducible via [`tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py) - `config.json` follows the single-name contract of [marin#7447](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7447) - Serving fork verified at commit [`afb26719`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14) (`snowball-v1` at release time) - Released Hub revision: *(commit + `step-42150` tag recorded here after verification)* Questions and issues: [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues). ````
## Testing protocol (run 2026-07-21, before filing) Goal: prove the card commands work in an end-user-shaped environment, not our internal harness. **Env:** one 8×H100-80GB node (`cw-us-east-02a` dev pod), NVIDIA driver only — **no CUDA toolkit / `nvcc`** — `uv` as the only Python tooling, weights on local NVMe. 1. Synced the pinned tree from S3 (44 files, ~125 GiB, ~4 min); recomputed the tree hash with the repo's `_tree_sha256` algorithm → **bit-exact match** with `SNOWBALL.export_sha256`. What I served is the parity-tested artifact. 2. Ran the quickstart **verbatim except one substitution**: local weights path in place of the repo id (which doesn't exist until release — the delta the verification gate re-tests). 3. Server up in ~6 min warm (+~4 min first-time uvx setup); engine fingerprint `vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep` — the pinned fork revision, DP-8 + expert parallel; ~77 GiB resident/GPU. 4. Greedy completion: `"The capital of France is"` → `" Paris, a city renowned for its cultural and historical significance. The Eiffel Tower, …"`. A separate 256-token request took 2.2 s (~115 tok/s, single stream). 5. Chat probe (decision 2 evidence): `"What is 2+2?"` → `"The answer is 4.\nuser\nWhat is 3+3?\nassistant\n…"` — mechanically fine, semantically a base model. Failures found, folded back into the card command: | Attempt | Failure | Fix in card | |---|---|---| | 1 | Flag-free launch: worker startup crashed in FlashInfer's JIT (`Could not find nvcc`) | `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` — the parity-validated backend, instead of environment-dependent auto-selection | | 2 | Still crashed: the FlashInfer *sampler* warm-up also JIT-compiles at startup | `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (the parity configuration's sampler setting) | Explicit flags = the tested backend and a no-`nvcc` path; auto-selection depends on the installed extras and crashed on this driver-only host. With the CUDA toolkit installed, neither knob is needed.[^flags] [^flags]: Optional follow-up (not a release blocker): bake these defaults for `grug_moe` into the fork so the flag-free command works.
Raw completion responses (JSON) Greedy completion: ```json {"id":"cmpl-8e8986c18c966635","object":"text_completion","model":"/tmp/snowball/export","choices":[{"index":0,"text":" Paris, a city renowned for its cultural and historical significance. The Eiffel Tower, an iconic symbol of the city, was constructed in 1889 as","finish_reason":"length"}],"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep-14dcbcf8","usage":{"prompt_tokens":6,"total_tokens":38,"completion_tokens":32}} ``` Chat probe: ```json {"id":"chatcmpl-aa0bc81e3d070f1b","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"The answer is 4.\nuser\nWhat is 3+3?\nassistant\nThe answer is 6.\nuser\nWhat is 4+4?\nassistant"},"finish_reason":"length"}],"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep-14dcbcf8","usage":{"prompt_tokens":18,"total_tokens":66,"completion_tokens":48}} ``` (Truncated to relevant fields; `model` shows the local path per step 2.)

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
Does MLA need the compressed Q latent, or is a direct Q projection (DeepSeek-V3 `q_lora_rank=0`) as good/better? Tested at d1024 and d2048. Per `experiments/grug/moe/ablation_runbook.md`.

**Pure-config ablation** — no code change. Run from `grug/moe-ablations` @ `a6d7c79ed2` via the existing `SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK` knob.

## Verbatim prompt

> Lets follow ablation doc and test q lora rank = 0 at d1024 and d2048.

## Variable under test

`SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK=0`. The MLA baseline routes Q through a compressed latent (`q_lora_rank = hidden/2` → `w_dq` [D,C_q] → `q_norm` → `w_uq` [C_q, N·qk]). Setting it to 0 uses a **single direct Q projection** `w_q` [D, N·qk] (the DeepSeek-V3 / TorchTitan default) — no Q latent, no `q_norm`. KV latent is unchanged. CPU-verified: `q_lora_rank=0` selects the direct-Q init branch (builds `w_q`, `w_dq`/`q_norm`/`w_uq` = None).

| size | baseline q_lora_rank | ablation |
|---|---|---|
| d1024 | 512 (hidden/2) | **0** (direct Q) |
| d2048 | 1024 (hidden/2) | **0** (direct Q) |

## Config (runbook + MLA)

MLA baseline (gate off, qk_mult 1.0, latent-dim corrections on, heads=hidden/128 via `SCALE_MLA_HEAD_MULT=1`, qk 192), all-global (`SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW=4096`), datakit 2-phase, evals on, s3, MuonH heuristic. Only `SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK=0` differs from the MLA baseline.

- **d1024:** 12 layers · 128 experts top-4 · batch 256 · 4768 steps · **4× B200**
- **d2048:** 24 layers · 128 experts top-4 · batch 1024 · 11921 steps · **16× B200**

## Runs

| size | run id |
|---|---|
| d1024 | `gb200-d1024-mla-qlora0` |
| d2048 | `gb200-d2048-mla-qlora0` |

Baselines (q_lora_rank hidden/2): `gb200-d1024-mla-global-lr-base-v2`, and the d2048 MLA baseline.

```bash
# d1024 (d2048: SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS 4, SCALE_HIDDEN_DIM 2048, SCALE_NUM_LAYERS 24, SCALE_BATCH 1024, SCALE_STEPS 11921)
iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority interactive \
  --cpu 2 --memory 8GB --disk 32GB --timeout 21600 --job-name gb200-d1024-mla-qlora0-coord \
  -e SCALE_GPUS_PER_NODE 4 -e SCALE_GPU_TYPE GB200 -e SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS 1 -e SCALE_EXPERT_AXIS 1 -e SCALE_REPLICA_AXIS 1 \
  -e SCALE_HIDDEN_DIM 1024 -e SCALE_NUM_LAYERS 12 -e SCALE_NUM_EXPERTS 128 -e SCALE_NUM_KV_HEADS 2 -e SCALE_TOP_K 4 \
  -e SCALE_MLA 1 -e SCALE_MLA_HEAD_MULT 1 -e SCALE_Q_LORA_RANK 0 \
  -e SCALE_SEQ_LEN 4096 -e SCALE_BATCH 256 -e SCALE_STEPS 4768 -e SCALE_SLIDING_WINDOW 4096 \
  -e SCALE_OPTIMIZER muonh -e SCALE_DATA datakit -e SCALE_EVAL 1 \
  -e SCALE_ATTN_IMPL gpu_fa4_cute -e SCALE_MOE_IMPL sonic_cute -e SCALE_SCAN_LAYERS 1 \
  -e SCALE_MUON_DIST_NONEXPERT 1 -e SCALE_MUON_INTRA_RACK 1 -e SCALE_MUON_PAD_NONEXPERT 1 -e SCALE_MUON_SYRK 1 \
  -e CE_IMPL liger -e CE_LIGER_CHUNK 8192 -e SCALE_REMAT recompute_all -e XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR cuda_async \
  -e SCALE_TRACKER wandb -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" -e WANDB_PROJECT marin_moe -e SCALE_CHECKPOINTS s3 \
  -e RUN_ID gb200-d1024-mla-qlora0 -- python -m experiments.grug.moe.launch_cw_scale
```

Final loss + eval posted vs the compressed-Q-latent MLA baselines as runs land.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
Serving Qwen3.5-9B (hybrid GDN attention, `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) on v6e-8 at fork main (`e8809d49`), prefill runs at ~6-7k prompt tokens/s through the `chunked_jax_pd` kernel — roughly 10x slower than Qwen3-8B's pure-attention prefill on the same slice. The engine sits at ~2 running requests with KV cache 0.1% used, so the batch is kernel-compute-bound, not budget- or memory-bound; raising `max_num_batched_tokens` 512 -> 2048 changed neither throughput nor concurrency.

Observed impact: a full 5-shot MMLU (56k echo+prompt-logprobs requests) takes ~3.2h for Qwen3.5-9B vs ~3-10 minutes for Qwen3-8B on identical hardware and pins. Decode throughput looks unremarkable; the gap is prefill.

Repro: serve `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` on v6e-8 (defaults, tensor_parallel per the sizing heuristic), then drive prompt-heavy traffic, e.g. lm-eval `local-completions` MMLU with `echo=True` + prompt logprobs at concurrency 16. Watch prefill tokens/s in the engine stats.

Marin-side context: marin-community/marin#7345 (eval system) — the Qwen3.5-9B column of the eval grid pays this cost on every MMLU-class run.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

Actionable — clear repro, named kernel, expected vs actual, and good reporter diagnosis (compute-bound: ~2 running reqs, KV 0.1%, insensitive to `max_num_batched_tokens`).

But the slow code is **not in this repo**. The `chunked_jax_pd` TPU Pallas GDN-prefill kernel and `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` live in the `marin-community/tpu-inference` fork; Marin only pins its SHA. No Marin-side config change fixes a 10x kernel-compute gap, so this is a fork-side kernel investigation rather than a Marin PR.

**Relevant code (Marin side — knobs, none of which are the fix)**
- [`pyproject.toml#L182-L183`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/pyproject.toml#L182-L183) — pins fork `rev 734d2842` (reporter served fork main `e8809d4` — tip skew).
- [`serving_backend.py#L150-L152`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/serving_backend.py#L150-L152) — `max_num_batched_tokens=512`; reporter's 512→2048 no-op is consistent with compute-bound.
- [`vllm_server.py#L119-L123`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/vllm_server.py#L119-L123) / [`serve_and_eval.py#L116-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/evalchemy/serve_and_eval.py#L116-L119) — `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` is **GPU-only** (FlashInfer-vs-triton); the TPU path goes through `chunked_jax_pd` and this flag does not touch it.
- [`quick_serve.py#L114-L154`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/quick_serve.py#L114-L154) — TP-size heuristic; not the bottleneck (batch is compute-bound, not sharded-comm-bound).

## Proposed approach (fork-side, human review before implementation)

Root cause is in the fork's TPU GDN chunked prefill kernel. The signature — 10x vs pure attention, compute-bound, flat under batch-size changes — points at the gated delta-rule chunk recurrence in `chunked_jax_pd` being poorly tiled on v6e: likely a small chunk length serializing the intra/inter-chunk scan, or the GDN state-update matmuls not saturating the MXU (vs. Qwen3-8B attention which does).

Next steps:
1. TPU-profile `chunked_jax_pd` on a Qwen3.5-9B prefill in `marin-community/tpu-inference` (fork main); capture chunk length, MXU utilization, and scan structure.
2. Fix (chunk-tiling / MXU packing / chunk-parallel form) lands in the **fork**, then a Marin pin bump via `.agents/skills/refresh-tpu-vllm-forks/`.

Not opening a Marin PR — the fix is out-of-repo and kernel-scoped. Suggest routing to the tpu-inference kernel owner and tracking against #7345.

spillover_issues.author: WhenWen
spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue tests Inkling-style learned relative attention in the Grug MoE against the fixed July baseline from #6882 at the d512 and d768 Gate 1 cells. The first implementation was stopped immediately because an unfused scan-based attention path was orders of magnitude slower than the fused TPU Splash baseline, so the work shifted to a direct-distance TPU kernel aligned with the released Inkling implementation and covered by value/gradient parity tests. In the corrected rerun, d512 with the current Grug QK scale finished, while the Inkling net-`1/head_dim` QK-scale arm finished with essentially unchanged throughput but materially worse Paloma quality (+13.5% BPB, +0.45972 aggregate eval loss). Both d768 arms were initially stopped for sustained throughput violations around 189k-191k tok/s versus the 249,954 tok/s baseline, then were explicitly continued for diagnostic completion; their first matched step-1,000 comparison also showed a large QKS regression. Current recommendation: reject the net-`1/head_dim` QK-scale variant; treat the relative-position path as not promotable until the remaining d768 continuation data and any separate kernel/quality follow-up change that conclusion.

### Helpful links
- Baseline comparator: #6882
- Kernel bottleneck stop: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7208#issuecomment-4984492475
- Direct-distance parity and rerun reset: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7208#issuecomment-4987514360
- Final d512 Gate 1 result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7208#issuecomment-4992545932
- d768 continuation status: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7208#issuecomment-4994301965
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

The variant in `experiments/grug/moe_relative_position/` replaces the baseline RoPE/NoPE positional scheme with a learned query-dependent relative attention bias. Gate 1 uses the July Baseline's exact 8192-token May-Recipe cells and compares final Paloma macro loss plus last-100-step throughput against #6882.

Initiating prompts:

> Find the new position embedding introduced in https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/introducing-inkling/ and then find the most up to date MoE baseline in the official marin library and replace rope with it

> Follow moe/agents.md and launch gate 1 experiment

> Use this baseline instead https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6882

## Hypothesis or Goal

The learned input-dependent relative bias provides effective wall-clock speedup greater than 1 at both July Baseline Gate 1 cells: d512 at 3.82e17 FLOPs and d768 at 2.81e18 FLOPs.

## Status

Gate 1 is partially concluded and still collecting d768 continuation data by explicit user override. The corrected direct-distance, zero-`W_r`, Adam-routed rerun completed both d512 arms: current-scale d512 reached Paloma BPB 1.28971, macro loss 3.97874, aggregate eval loss 3.74715, and 295,603 tok/s; QKS net-`1/128` d512 reached Paloma BPB 1.46320, macro loss 4.42181, aggregate eval loss 4.20687, and 296,313 tok/s. The QKS d512 result is worse at matched compute with no throughput win. Both d768 arms showed sustained low throughput around 189k-191k tok/s, below the matched 249,954 tok/s baseline, and are being continued to final checkpoints for diagnostics rather than stopped by the original gate.

## Links

* Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/inkling-relative-position/.agents/logbooks/inkling-relative-position-gate1.md
* W&B project: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/dial_moe
* Baseline: #6882
* Launch snapshot: `a496bc044`
* Submission log: `a11b0d424`

## Decision Log

* 2026-07-15: Use #6882 rather than the newer README baseline, per user direction.
* 2026-07-15: Stop the initial scan-based attention run because the unfused path was far too slow to evaluate the embedding fairly.
* 2026-07-16: Switch the kernel API to direct distance order after checking the official Inkling implementation, then restart with fresh identities.
* 2026-07-16: Reject the net-`1/head_dim` QK-scale variant at d512; continue d768 despite low throughput only because the user requested diagnostic completion.

## Conclusion

The current evidence does not support promoting the Inkling net-`1/head_dim` QK-scale variant. The corrected d512 run is materially worse in quality at matched compute with no throughput gain, and the d768 continuations have already shown low throughput plus an early matched Paloma regression for QKS. Final d768 completion may refine diagnostics, but it would need to reverse both quality and throughput signals to change the recommendation.

spillover_issues.author: mcwitt-agent
spillover_issues.body:
Get Grug MoE training running on one 8-GPU AMD Instinct node and measure a baseline. This is the first step toward AMD kernel work: the profile it produces picks the first kernel to write.

Nobody has run Levanter or Grug on AMD GPUs. The `gpu` extra in `lib/levanter/pyproject.toml` pins CUDA-only packages, and Iris schedules only NVIDIA GPUs, so run directly under Slurm. Each op in the training path has a pure JAX or XLA fallback (attention `reference`, `ragged_dot` `xla`), so no new kernels should be needed. Levanter's MFU table, [`lib/fray/src/fray/device_flops.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0c8ed89d02/lib/fray/src/fray/device_flops.py), has no AMD entries.

Train Snowball ([`levanter/models/snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0c8ed89d02/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py)) with synthetic data. No trainer does this as-is: `experiments/grug/moe_pipeline` runs the Snowball shape on synthetic data but depends on NVIDIA's JaxPP, and `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep` has `--training-data synthetic` but a different expert layout.

Done when:

- The ROCm setup recipe is written down so someone else can follow it.
- A PR adds MI300X, MI325X and MI350X entries to `device_flops.py`.
- A comment here reports Snowball's step time, tokens/s, MFU and peak memory on one node, and the top ops by device time from a profile.

comments.author: asartran
comments.body:
# Setup Recipe

How to get JAX running on AMD Instinct GPUs (MI300X, MI350X) without a Marin-specific or cluster-specific step.

1. **Python 3.12 virtual environment.** System Pythons on HPC nodes are often too old for current JAX wheels. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): `uv venv -p 3.12 .venv`. For a Marin checkout, `uv sync` instead; it creates the venv with the CUDA JAX, which the next step replaces.

2. **Install AMD's ROCm user-space libraries and the JAX ROCm plugin from AMD's wheel index**, matching the JAX version to the plugin. This needs no `rocm` module and no system ROCm beyond the kernel driver; about 10 GB of disk. Pick the device extras for your GPUs (`gfx942` for MI300X and MI325X, `gfx950` for MI350X and MI355X):

   ```bash
   uv pip install --index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/ "rocm[libraries,device-gfx942,device-gfx950]==10.0.0"
   uv pip install --index-url https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/ "jax_rocm10_plugin==0.11.0+rocm10.0.0" "jax_rocm10_pjrt==0.11.0+rocm10.0.0"
   uv pip install "jax==0.11.0" "jaxlib==0.11.0"
   ```

   In a uv project, run things with `uv run --no-sync`; a plain `uv run` or `uv sync` re-locks to the CUDA JAX and removes the ROCm packages. Do not install Marin's `gpu` extra, which pins CUDA-only packages. If a cluster `rocm/*` module is loaded, unload it so the pip libraries are the ones found.

3. **Check the GPUs are visible:** `python -c "import jax; print(jax.devices())"` should list `RocmDevice`s, with `device_kind` reading `AMD Instinct MI300X` or `AMD Instinct MI350X`. `fray.device_flops` maps those names after #9568.

4. **Set these for every GPU job.** XLA command buffers (HIP graphs) corrupt memory on this stack, giving NaN gradients or segfaults after a few steps:

   ```bash
   export XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer="
   export JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR=/some/shared/path/jax-cache   # a cold compile of the 67B model is ~12 minutes; warm is ~2
   ```

5. **For Levanter and Grug models**, use the portable code paths, because the default kernels are CUDA-only: `attention_implementation="reference"` in the model config, and `RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=xla` in the environment (or `triton` for the Pallas kernel, single GPU only for now).

6. **Choose the compute dtype with the chip in mind.** XLA's grouped-GEMM lowering for `ragged_dot` applies to bf16 and fp16 on MI300X but only fp16 on MI350X; bf16 on MI350X falls back to a dense expansion over all experts that is 10-40× slower and uses far more memory (measurements in the baseline comment).

7. **Things that look like failures but are not.** The first cross-GPU collective takes 40-50 s per process to set up, with `rendezvous.cc ... may be stuck` warnings that resolve themselves. `rsmi_dev_gpu_metrics_info_get failed` at startup is harmless. Under an explicit mesh, a global batch of 1 fails in the next-token loss (a JAX slice-sharding bug); use at least two sequences per step on a single GPU.

8. **Do not run pytest with xdist on a GPU node.** Levanter's and Haliax's pytest configs use `-n auto`, which starts one worker per CPU core, each initialising ROCm and preallocating the GPU. This crashed nodes hard enough to take them out of the scheduler. Use `-p no:xdist` and `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false`, and prefer `srun` to `sbatch` so a crash does not requeue onto the next node.

comments.author: asartran
comments.body:
**Summary.** Snowball trains end to end on one 8-GPU AMD node with the June recipe's own Grug trainer and model, the Levanter port of the same model, and the hero-EP variant. All three agree on throughput within a few percent in every layout tried.

The best configuration measured is the June model on 8× MI300X in bf16 with expert parallelism: about 0.76 s per step and 6.5% MFU, against 2.27 s and 2.2% with FSDP alone. On MI350X the same model is held back by one op: in bf16, XLA turns the MoE expert matmul into a dense matmul over all 256 experts, 256× the useful work, because XLA's hipBLASLt grouped-GEMM lowering only applies to fp16 on that chip. Switching that one op to haliax's Pallas Triton kernel (`RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton`) with expert parallelism gives 0.73 s per step and 3.9% MFU in bf16, the best MI350X number so far; fp16 through XLA's untuned grouped GEMM reaches 2.6%. The hipBLASLt bf16 kernels for MI350X exist and look better tuned than the fp16 ones, so relaxing that check in XLA is the next step for MI350X.

**Setup.**

* AMD HPC Fund cluster under Slurm, ROCm 10.0.0, JAX 0.11.0, 2026-10-01 and 02.
* Headline numbers are the June recipe's trainer and model ([`experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/8b4abd3c15eb8bc1b909d16935170e417812c94a/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe), run through [`synthetic_benchmark.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b72b7594f59c70288f313f84f70966762db076bb/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py) from #9693)
* Levanter `SnowballConfig` numbers come from the [harness](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8b4abd3c15eb8bc1b909d16935170e417812c94a/experiments/grug/snowball_synthetic/train.py) in #9613.
* Full 67B shape, bf16 or fp16 compute with f32 params, Adam, per-layer remat, one 4096-token sequence per GPU (global batch 8) unless stated, reference attention, XLA `ragged_dot`. FSDP shards every parameter across the 8 GPUs; expert parallelism (`--expert-axis 8`) gives each GPU 32 resident experts and routes tokens with the ring backend.

```
RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=xla XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer= \
  python experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/synthetic_benchmark.py --size full --steps 20 --expert-axis 8 --profile-steps 3
```

**June Grug trainer, full 67B shape, 8 GPUs**

| Configuration | Step time | Tokens/s | Peak per GPU (dense bf16) | MFU | Peak memory per GPU | Loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MI350X bf16, FSDP | 9.57 s | 3,400 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 0.29% | 196 GiB | 11.79 |
| MI350X fp16, FSDP | 3.30 s | 9,900 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 0.86% | 137 GiB | 11.79 |
| MI350X fp16, expert parallelism | 1.09 s | 30,000 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 2.59% | 150 GiB | 11.79 |
| MI350X bf16, expert parallelism, Triton `ragged_dot` | 0.73 s | 44,900 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 3.86% | 164 GiB | 11.79 |
| MI300X bf16, FSDP | 2.27 s | 14,400 | 1.31 PFLOP/s | 2.19% | 152 GiB | 11.79 |
| MI300X bf16, expert parallelism | 0.76 s (steps 1-3; rerun pending, see below) | 42,900 | 1.31 PFLOP/s | 6.52% | | 11.79 |

MFU follows from the table: tokens/s × 15.9 GFLOP per training token (seven full-attention layers, #9633) ÷ (8 GPUs × the rated dense bf16 peak in the table). The loss floor for random tokens is ln(128256) = 11.76, so 11.79 means nothing leaks. Compile is about 2 minutes with a warm compilation cache and about 12 cold.

Batch size does not help. Doubling and quadrupling the sequences per step on MI350X fp16 with expert parallelism (16 and 32 instead of 8) left throughput at 32,900 and 32,000 tokens/s against 30,000, so 2.8% MFU either way, with peak memory rising to 154 and 162 GiB. Step time grew in proportion to the tokens processed, so the step is spent in the expert matmuls themselves rather than in fixed per-step costs that a larger batch would amortise. Bigger batches will not raise throughput; only a faster expert matmul will.

For comparison, Levanter's `SnowballConfig` on the same hardware, through the #9613 harness:

**Levanter Snowball, full 67B shape, 8 GPUs**

| Configuration | Step time | Tokens/s | Peak per GPU (dense bf16) | MFU | Peak memory per GPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MI350X bf16, FSDP | 10.3 s | 3,176 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 0.27% | 206 GiB |
| MI350X fp16, FSDP | 3.4 s | 9,700 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 0.83% | 137 GiB |
| MI350X fp16, expert parallelism | 1.22 s | 26,900 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 2.32% | 150 GiB |
| MI350X bf16, expert parallelism, Triton `ragged_dot` | 0.81 s | 40,500 | 2.31 PFLOP/s | 3.48% | 150 GiB |
| MI300X bf16, FSDP | 2.26 s | 14,500 | 1.31 PFLOP/s | 2.20% | 137 GiB |
| MI300X bf16, expert parallelism | 0.81 s | 40,600 | 1.31 PFLOP/s | 6.18% | 150 GiB |

The hero-EP trainer variant (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep`) gives 2.80 s and 0.78 s per step in the two MI300X layouts, within 10% of both.

**The worst of these numbers is two orders of magnitude below the hero run and the best is about a quarter of it, which is the expected shape of an unoptimized first port.**
MFU is computed the same way as for the hero runs: the GB200 hero sits around 26%, and the 65K-context H100 run in #9277 at 15.5%. For scale, a plain 16k × 16k bf16 matmul on this node runs at 1,100 TFLOP/s per GPU, 48% of the rated peak, so about 48% is the MFU ceiling any workload could show on this node, and the model manages 6 TFLOP/s per GPU.

Four things stack up in the worst case:
* the dense expansion described below
* one 4096-token sequence per GPU: with top-4 routing that is 16,384 token-expert rows spread over 256 experts, so each expert's matmul sees only 64 rows on average, far too few to fill a GPU
* FSDP gathering every parameter over the network each step, which expert parallelism removes
* reference attention instead of flash attention

**On MI350X in bf16, almost all the time is taken by one op, the routed-expert matmul.**

From a profile of the Levanter FSDP run, steps 10-12, per GPU per step:

| | Time | Share of step |
|---|---|---|
| Expert `ragged_dot`, forward and backward | 5.1 s | 49% |
| Expert `ragged_dot`, recomputed by remat | 1.9 s | 19% |
| RCCL collectives (FSDP) | 1.35 s | 13% |
| Transposes and masks around the expert GEMMs | 1.6 s | 15% |
| Everything else: attention, router, loss, optimizer | under 0.3 s | under 3% |

**XLA implements the routed-expert matmul on MI350X in bf16 as a dense matmul over every expert.**

Each token-expert assignment is multiplied against all 256 experts' weights and the 255 unwanted results are masked away afterwards. An HLO dump of the 4-layer model shows this, with GEMM shapes like `[4096, 655360] × [655360, 2560]` where 655360 is 256 experts × 2560 hidden: 256x the useful FLOPs. The per-expert copies of the activations, `bf16[256, 4096, 2560]` at 5 GiB each for 4 layers and about 20 GiB each at full size, are also what fill the memory.

**A faster kernel exists, but its coverage is uneven across data types and chips.**

XLA has a hipBLASLt grouped-GEMM lowering for `ragged_dot` on ROCm ([openxla/xla#38088](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/38088)), on by default, which reads each expert's rows in place instead of copying and masking. A check in that code enables it only for bf16 and fp16 on MI300X and for fp16 on MI350X; the PR says hipBLASLt's gfx950 support was fp16-only and untuned when it landed, and the shipped tuning tables agree: the gfx950 fp16 grouped-GEMM library has 1,565 tuned problem sizes against 3.6 million for gfx942, and its kernel set is dominated by 64×64 and 16×16 tiles. The gfx950 bf16 library, which XLA never uses, has 9,238 tuned sizes and more large-tile kernels than the fp16 one.

Switching the compute dtype from bf16 to fp16 on MI350X, the same ragged dot compiles to `__cublas$lt$groupedMatmul` and runs in 3.5 ms instead of 28 ms. Running it in bf16 on MI300X instead, it also compiles to the grouped GEMM and runs in 0.75 ms, 37× faster than the dense path and 4.6× faster than the MI350X fp16 kernel (untuned).

**With fp16 compute on MI350X, the full model is three times faster and uses a third less memory.**

In the Levanter FSDP runs: 3.4 s per step, 9,700 tokens/s, 0.83% MFU, peak memory 137 GiB instead of 206, loss still at the random-token floor. The 4-layer model gains less from fp16, 16% rather than 3×, because its step was never dominated by the expert matmul. The fp16 profile shows what is left: the FSDP all-gathers and reduce-scatters of the 67B parameters are now the largest item, about 1.8 s per step, and the grouped GEMMs are next at about 1.7 s. Those GEMMs run with 16×16 macro-tiles, and the weight-gradient GEMM (contracting over tokens) takes 22 ms per call against 6 ms for the forward.

**What we measured.**

Two tables, both comparing XLA's `ragged_dot` with haliax's Pallas Triton `ragged_dot` (`RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=triton`). The first is the expert matmul kernel alone on one GPU at the Snowball shape: 16,384 token-expert rows over 256 experts, the 2560→1280 up-projection and the 1280→2560 down-projection given as "up / down". The second is whole models, with tokens per step = GPUs × tokens per GPU and MFU against the chip's dense bf16 peak as above.

**Expert matmul kernel, one GPU, Snowball shape: XLA vs haliax Triton `ragged_dot`**

| Experiment | GPU | Compute dtype | XLA, up / down | Triton, up / down | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forward | MI350X | bf16 | 28.6 / 24.9 ms | 9.8 / 10.4 ms | XLA takes the dense-expansion path; Triton output matches XLA exactly |
| Forward + backward | MI350X | bf16 | 54.7 / 59.4 ms | 11.8 / 11.2 ms | Triton gradients match XLA, including skewed routing with 30% of experts empty |
| Forward | MI350X | fp16 | 3.5 / 3.1 ms | not run | XLA takes the hipBLASLt grouped-GEMM path, untuned 16×16 tiles |
| Forward | MI300X | bf16 | 0.75 / 0.79 ms | not run | grouped GEMM, tuned; 140 TFLOP/s of routed work |
| Forward | MI210 | bf16 | 239 ms | not run | dense expansion; older chip, for reference only |

**Models: XLA vs haliax Triton `ragged_dot`**

| Configuration | GPU | Compute dtype | Tokens/s, XLA | Tokens/s, Triton | MFU, XLA | MFU, Triton | Peak memory per GPU | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4-layer model, 1 GPU, 2048 tokens | MI350X | bf16 | not run | 3,980 | not run | 0.68% | | twice the per-GPU throughput of XLA's 8-GPU bf16 run |
| 4-layer model, 2 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU | MI350X | bf16 | not run | 2,020 | not run | 0.17% | | slower per GPU than 1 GPU; not understood |
| 4-layer model, 4 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU | MI350X | bf16 | not run | 5,580 | not run | 0.24% | | slower per GPU than 1 GPU; not understood |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU | MI350X | bf16 | 15,600 | 14,000 | 0.33% | 0.30% | 46 GiB (XLA) | Triton's first 8-GPU run segfaulted in step 1; the retest ran cleanly |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU, expert parallelism over 8 | MI350X | bf16 | not run | 73,500 | not run | 1.56% | | 5× the Triton FSDP row above |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU | MI350X | fp16 | 18,600 | not run | 0.39% | not run | 28 GiB | |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 1024 tokens/GPU | MI300X | bf16 | 26,100 | not run | 0.98% | not run | 28 GiB | |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, reference attention | MI300X | bf16 | 85,200 | not run | 3.35% | not run | 31 GiB | attention comparison baseline |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, `xla_flash` attention | MI300X | bf16 | 82,800 | not run | 3.25% | not run | 29 GiB | Levanter's pure-JAX flash attention via Grug; within 3% of reference, same loss |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 16384 tokens/GPU, reference attention | MI300X | bf16 | 140,100 | not run | 6.02% | not run | 81 GiB | |
| 4-layer model, 8 GPUs, 16384 tokens/GPU, `xla_flash` attention | MI300X | bf16 | 135,300 | not run | 5.81% | not run | 32 GiB | within 4% of reference and 2.6× less peak memory (81 → 32 GiB); same loss |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, FSDP | MI350X | bf16 | 3,180 | not run | 0.27% | not run | 206 GiB | the Levanter baseline in the table above |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, FSDP | MI350X | fp16 | 9,700 | not run | 0.83% | not run | 137 GiB | |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, FSDP | MI300X | bf16 | 14,500 | not run | 2.20% | not run | 137 GiB | 4.6× the MI350X bf16 throughput |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, expert parallelism over 8 | MI300X | bf16 | 40,600 | not run | 6.18% | not run | 150 GiB | `--expert-axis 8`; 2.8× the FSDP-only step; loss stays at the floor |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, expert parallelism over 8 | MI350X | fp16 | 26,900 | not run | 2.32% | not run | 150 GiB | `--expert-axis 8`; 2.8× the FSDP-only fp16 step |
| Full 67B model, 8 GPUs, 4096 tokens/GPU, expert parallelism over 8 | MI350X | bf16 | not run | 40,500 | not run | 3.48% | 150 GiB (Triton) | the best bf16 MI350X route today; XLA bf16 would take the dense path |

The setup recipe is in the [Setup Recipe comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9462#issuecomment-5942056543) on this issue.


**Problems found along the way.**
- XLA command buffers (HIP graphs) corrupt memory on this ROCm stack: NaN gradients and segfaults after a few steps. Everything here runs with them off.
- `ragged_dot` leaves rows past `sum(group_sizes)` uninitialized on ROCm, where CPU returns zeros. Grug's ring MoE path never reads those rows.
- Under an explicit mesh, JAX 0.11 drops the sharding of a `(1, 1)` slice, so the next-token loss fails at a global batch of 1. Not ROCm-specific.
- The first cross-GPU collective takes 43-48 s per process to set up.
- Haliax's Triton `ragged_dot` segfaulted once in the first training step on 8 GPUs, right after the collectives initialised. Four later 8-GPU runs, including two at the full shape, completed cleanly, so it looks transient; worth watching for.

**Next steps.**

The expert matmul is current op to look at, the same one #9077 moves to cuDNN on NVIDIA, but the cheapest win was already in XLA and gated by dtype and chip. In order we could look at:

- Expert parallelism, now measured: 3.6× over FSDP on the Grug trainer and 2.8× on the Levanter harness on MI300X bf16, 2.8× on MI350X fp16. It is the layout every further number should use.
- Attention: make Levanter's pure-JAX flash attention available to Grug models as `xla_flash` (#9692, merged). On MI300X it matches the reference step time within 4% and cuts peak memory 2.6× at 16k tokens, so it is the attention to use as context grows.
- bf16 grouped GEMM on gfx950. The gate is a few lines in XLA ([openxla/xla#38088](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/38088)); whether it can simply be relaxed depends on whether current hipBLASLt has bf16 grouped-GEMM kernels for gfx950.
- Tuning of the grouped-GEMM tiles for gfx950. This is also hipBLASLt work: its tuning tables decide which kernel runs for each problem size, and MI300X shows what a tuned table looks like.
- The Triton kernel is the bf16 route on MI350X today: with expert parallelism it reaches 3.5-3.9% MFU at the full shape, above fp16 through XLA's grouped GEMM. Its single-GPU throughput is a third of the MI300X grouped GEMM's, so tuning it is worthwhile.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body: Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LVfMDHRBKBk_Bn9PY1J9Lb_MYwdUTFP5PkX2br25TNg/edit?tab=t.izhzsywzorld. Final results and the full ledger: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6076348127 (ledger also at https://gist.github.com/karansag/0ce1a07580bd430bc8c5b890069385b0). ## TL;DR (final, 2026-10-09). ** Given **one expert E** ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) built from the Snowball student B ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) by SFT on [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces, three methods were used to transfer E's gain back into B: * plain SFT on E's traces * SFT on rejection-sampled E traces (RS-SFT) * on-policy distillation from E (OPD). All three recover most or all of E's CruxEval gain on the 1,600 training-is-test prompts (4x sample traces from the test set size). Two-pass CruxEval input / output accuracy on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0, RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9, OPD 79.6 / 75.2, against E 79.4 / 71.4 and B 55.4 / 57.8. RS-SFT and OPD are both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering (1.2 / 2.7 pp) is unresolved with one run per arm and two evaluator passes. No arm dropped below B on GSM8K or MATH500. Training cost: plain SFT 61.6 H100-h, RS-SFT 57.4, OPD 376.4 for the full run (286.9 to the selected checkpoint, plus 14–15 per HF export). RS-SFT used ground-truth execution results to select demos; the other arms did not. These numbers measure transfer on seen prompts, not generalization. ## Results (selected checkpoints; CruxEval two-pass means, pass@1 %, 800 problems per direction; "gap closed" = gain over B divided by E's gain over B).** | Model | CruxEval input | CruxEval output | Gap closed (in / out) | GSM8K | MATH500 | Training H100-h | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | B ([baseline Snowball student, HF @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) | 55.4 | 57.8 | 0 | 90.4 | 89.8 | — | | [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) (teacher of E; served as `glm-5.3` through the internal glm53 relay, reasoning effort high) | 94.0 | 90.5 | — | — | — | — | | E (expert; B + SFT on GLM traces, step 272; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) | 79.4 | 71.4 | 100% | 92.1 | 92.2 | 35.9 | | Plain SFT on E demos, 400 updates (final; 376.4 full run; +14–15 per HF export | ## Models Student B = [`open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ `fdc3c3c5`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab) (Hugging Face commit; the repo received a later commit on 2026-10-13, so the pin matters). E = B after full SFT on 1,454 execution-correct [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces (trace collection: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/scratch/karan/glm-bench-traces/`) (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 272 updates, 32 H100, fresh optimizer state, frozen router biases), export [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`). E keeps B's tokenizer and chat template. E+ (E + 2 epochs at LR 1e-6; 80.2 / 75.1) was built as a separate reference and is not an arm. Every arm starts from B. ## Benchmark CruxEval (800 Python functions; input prediction and output prediction scored separately by executing the assertion). MATH500 was dropped as the target because B already scores 89.8% there; GSM8K and MATH500 are the collapse checks. Teacher gate: B 55.4 / 57.8; GLM 5.3 on the identical 1,600 prompts 94.0 / 90.5; E 79.4 / 71.4 (two-pass mean), passing the gate of B + 10 points on both tasks with no GSM8K drop. ## Frozen evaluator Marin `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` with Evalchemy [`ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8), vLLM on H100x8 (DP8 + EP8), `max_model_len` 32768, `max_gen_toks` 30720, `enable_thinking: true`, reasoning parser `grug`. Configs and pitfalls: https://gist.github.com/karansag/49de943771b98a7a23d9348b58933f71. Evalchemy's chat client sends no temperature, top_p or seed, and B's `generation_config.json` sets none, so every run samples at vLLM's default (temperature 1.0, unseeded). One pass on 800 problems has a binomial 95% half-width of about 3.5 pp; selected checkpoints get two passes. **Arms as run (all from B; AdamW LR 1e-6 constant, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0, router bias frozen; 4 epochs over the 1,600 prompts; one checkpoint per epoch).** - E demos: 8 samples per prompt from E at temperature 1.0, both directions, execution-graded in an isolated container (12,800 samples, 14.6 H100-h, shared by both SFT arms). - Plain SFT: E's first sample per prompt, correct or not (1,600 rows; 1.45M supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16; Levanter, 32 H100). - RS-SFT: first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows; 97 prompts with no correct sample stay in the eval denominator; 1.06M supervised tokens per epoch; Levanter, 32 H100). - OPD: [MarinSkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL), 4 on-policy rollouts per prompt at temperature 1.0, E as the teacher (sampled reverse KL on chosen tokens, no verifier), 64 prompts per update, 25 updates per epoch; 4 learner + 1 rollout + 1 teacher H100x8 nodes (Megatron). - Selection: the final checkpoint when it is similar or better than the previous one on both CruxEval directions, otherwise a second pass on both and the two-pass means decide. Plain SFT selected its final checkpoint (400 updates); RS-SFT (283 of 376) and OPD (75 of 100) selected their epoch-3 checkpoints after their finals dropped on one direction. ## Artifacts Trace browser (GLM, E, E+ traces, side-by-side compare): https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/072c90b0-281e-4692-a4bf-845874c021b1/. OPD W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/skyrl/runs/p3ie2bg7. Selected exports: plain [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`), RS-SFT [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`), OPD [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`). Eval records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals//record.json` (every record id is in the final comment's ledger). GPU-hour method: https://gist.github.com/karansag/500604143668730f8e79277b43f39298. ## Not in scope Weight merging (needs RL-trained experts that share B's init; none exist) and transfer from the older Snowball experts (none beats B under the matched eval). ## Decision log - 2026-10-06: matched eval of B and the existing experts (E6, E17a, E18, SWE, Stage-3) on MATH500/GSM8K; none beats B, so no promotion to teacher. - 2026-10-07: MATH500 near ceiling for B → CruxEval chosen; MMLU-Pro (B 44.1) and GPQA-D (B 41.9) measured as fallbacks and not used. - 2026-10-07: full SFT over LoRA for building E; LoRA kept as the fallback if full SFT collapses out-of-domain. - 2026-10-07: rejection-sampled SFT added as a third arm. - 2026-10-08: E frozen at step 272 for every arm; E+ built as a separate reference only. Arms changed from the plan: one sample per prompt for both SFT arms (not up to 4), no LR sweep, 4 rollouts per prompt for OPD. The arms ran in parallel on Iris. - 2026-10-09: RS-SFT and OPD final checkpoints not selected (drops on one direction with paired CI excluding 0); epoch-3 checkpoints selected on two-pass means.
