comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Teacher training and three transfer arms make this a gated experiment. As of 23:29 UTC, the owner has submitted the W&B-corrected teacher retry; startup, optimizer progress, and export remain unconfirmed ([latest status](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6048938002)). No open PR targets #9920, while the owner is already preparing the recipe on `task/133`; the earlier coding-teacher spike [#9528](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9528) ended without a usable MOPD transfer result.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494) — shared SFT specification and training setup
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150) — versioned SkyRL experiment and export contract
- [`experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147) — shared evaluation launch path

# Proposed Fix

1. Follow the submitted teacher retry through a completed update, full training, and verified HF exports. Evaluate the planned exports with the frozen CruxEval/GSM8K configuration. Stop the transfer arms unless E clears the stated +10-point gate on both CruxEval directions without a GSM8K drop beyond noise.
2. Pin E, B, prompt IDs, tokenizer/template, grader, evaluator, and one eight-sample-per-prompt teacher generation artifact. Build unfiltered SFT from samples 1–4 and rejection-sampled SFT from up to four execution-correct samples. Record missing-correct-sample prompts, actual supervised tokens, and teacher-generation GPU-hours; a matched prompt set alone does not equalize training tokens.
3. Start OPD from the same B and prompts. Check teacher/student token-score alignment and one update plus export before the full run. Match the planned sweep and student update budget across arms, and record teacher-scoring GPU-hours separately.
4. Evaluate every selected arm twice with the same pinned evaluator on CruxEval input, CruxEval output, and GSM8K. Report each arm's accuracy, `(arm − B) / (E − B)` per direction, run-to-run spread, prompts and tokens consumed, and total GPU-hours. Label gains as transfer on the trained test prompts; this protocol cannot establish held-out generalization.

comments.body:
🤖 Final results: SFT vs rejection-sampled SFT vs on-policy distillation for transferring the CruxEval expert back into B

TL;DR. All three arms recover most or all of the expert's CruxEval gain. Every arm trains on prompts drawn from the same 1,600 the evaluator scores (800 input-prediction and 800 output-prediction problems; plain SFT and OPD use all 1,600, RS-SFT the 1,503 with an execution-correct E sample), so this is transfer on seen prompts. Two-pass means on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0 (400 updates), RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9 (283 updates), OPD 79.6 / 75.2 (75 updates); the expert E scores 79.4 / 71.4 and B scores 55.4 / 57.8 (CruxEval input / output, pass@1 on 800 problems each). RS-SFT's two-pass means are 1.2 / 2.7 pp above OPD's; two passes on one run per arm do not resolve that ordering. Both are above plain SFT by 5.7–6.9 pp on input and 3.2–5.9 pp on output. Training cost: OPD 287 H100-h from allocation to the selected checkpoint (376 for the full 4-epoch run); plain SFT 62 and RS-SFT 57 for their full 4-epoch runs (the RS candidate is update 283 of 376 and was not timed separately). RS-SFT also used ground-truth execution results to pick its demos, which the other arms did not have. No arm dropped below B on GSM8K (B 90.4) or MATH500 (B 89.8); OPD 75 scores 90.4 on MATH500, 1.8 below E, inside MATH500's binomial 95% half-width of about 2.6 pp at n=500. These numbers do not measure generalization to unseen prompts.

Setup (the design doc is linked from the issue body).

- Student B: [`open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ `fdc3c3c5`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab).
- Expert E: B after full SFT on 1,454 [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces, LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, step 272 (35.9 H100-h); export [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`). E+ (E + 2 epochs at 1e-6, 80.2 / 75.1) is a reference only.
- Evaluator: Evalchemy [ae362881](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8) (corrected 2026-10-13: the revision that actually ran is `ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8`, recorded in every record's `eval_runtime` field; `c131e5ab` was the code constant in `eval_policy.py`, which the launcher did not use. The scorer and sampling settings are the ones at ae362881 throughout, so no number changes.), vLLM H100x8, 32,768 context, 30,720 generation cap, thinking enabled, unseeded sampling at vLLM's default temperature 1.0 (the lm-eval chat client sends no sampling parameters). One pass has a binomial 95% half-width of about 3.5 pp at n=800 (p≈0.55) and 3.0 pp at p≈0.75. Paired deltas use a problem-resampling bootstrap conditional on the sampled completions. Gist of all evaluator configs: https://gist.github.com/karansag/49de943771b98a7a23d9348b58933f71.
- Matched AdamW hyperparameters across arms, in different implementations (Levanter for the SFT arms, Megatron for OPD): LR 1e-6 constant, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0, router bias frozen (E froze it too; all exports verified to carry B's 26 router-bias tensors).
- Plain SFT: B + 4 epochs on E's first sample per prompt (1,600 rows, unfiltered), batch 16, 32 H100. 1,452,363 supervised tokens per epoch.
- RS-SFT: all 12,800 E samples (k=8) execution-graded in an isolated container; first correct sample per prompt kept. 1,503 of 1,600 prompts covered (774 input / 729 output); the 97 uncovered prompts stay in the eval denominator. 4 epochs, 376 updates. 1,056,479 supervised tokens per epoch.
- OPD: MarinSkyRL, B samples 4 rollouts per prompt at temperature 1.0, E scores them (sampled reverse KL on the chosen tokens, coefficient 1.0, reward replaced by the distillation signal, no verifier). 64 prompts per update, 25 updates per epoch, 4 epochs. 4 learner nodes (PP2 × EP8) + 1 rollout node + 1 teacher node, all H100x8.
- Selection procedure used (the rule 'prefer the final checkpoint when similar or better on both directions' was agreed before the final checkpoints were scored; the operational reading of similar as 'paired 95% CI includes 0' was fixed while applying it): if the final checkpoint is similar or better than the previous one on both CruxEval directions on the first pass, select it; otherwise run a second pass on both checkpoints and choose on the two-pass means. GSM8K and MATH500 run on the selected checkpoint and on any terminal checkpoint that lost the selection.

Results. CruxEval pass@1 (%), input / output. "Gap closed" is the gain over B divided by E's two-pass gain over B (24.06 pp input, 13.63 pp output). GSM8K (flexible-extract, 0-shot) and MATH500 are single pass for every model.

| Model | Input | Output | Gap closed | GSM8K | MATH500 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B | 55.4 | 57.8 | 0 | 90.4 | 89.8 |
| E (CruxEval 2-pass mean) | 79.4 | 71.4 | 100% | 92.1 | 92.2 |
| GLM 5.3 (teacher of E) | 94.0 | 90.5 | — | — | — |
| Plain SFT, 400 updates (2-pass mean) | 73.9 | 72.0 | 77% / 104% | 94.0 | 92.6 |
| RS-SFT, 283 updates (epoch 3) (2-pass mean) | 80.8 | 77.9 | 106% / 148% | 93.5 | 93.6 |
| OPD, 75 updates (epoch 3) (2-pass mean) | 79.6 | 75.2 | 101% / 128% | 92.5 | 90.4 |

Learning curves (single pass per checkpoint; the training trajectory, not the selection basis):

| Arm | Epoch 1 | Epoch 2 | Epoch 3 | Epoch 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain SFT (101/201/301/400 updates) | 69.6 / 67.5 | 73.5 / 69.9 | 69.4 / 71.8 | 74.8 / 71.3 |
| RS-SFT (95/189/283/376 updates) | 75.5 / 72.0 | 82.0 / 75.8 | 81.4 / 77.1 | 77.0 / 76.5 |
| OPD (25/50/75/100 updates) | 74.9 / 68.9 | 81.8 / 75.8 | 79.0 / 76.8 | 80.9 / 72.3 |

Selection. Plain SFT's final checkpoint was similar or better than its epoch-3 checkpoint on both directions (+5.4 / −0.5 pp), so it was selected and repeated (second pass 73.1 / 72.8). RS-SFT's final checkpoint was 4.4 pp below epoch 3 on input, and OPD's final checkpoint was 4.5 pp below epoch 3 on output, each with a paired CI excluding 0. Both arms got a second pass on their last two checkpoints. RS-SFT: 376 updates 76.1 / 76.2 against 283 updates 80.8 / 77.9 (two-pass means); the final is lower on both directions, so 283 was selected. OPD: 100 updates 79.875 / 72.0 against 75 updates 79.625 / 75.19; input differs by 0.25 pp and the final is 3.19 pp lower on output, so 75 was selected. The terminal checkpoints are reported in the curve table, not as the method result. The second passes reuse the same runs, so the four pass pairings per arm are one comparison, not four. Same-checkpoint pass pairs moved by up to 3.1 pp (OPD 75 output: 76.75 on pass 1, 73.6 on pass 2, paired CI [−6.0, −0.25]), so the conditional problem-bootstrap intervals do not capture all generation variability; two repeats are too few to estimate it. The final-checkpoint drops are therefore suggestive, not established.

Paired comparisons at the selected checkpoints (pass 1 vs pass 1; 95% bootstrap CI): RS-SFT 283 vs OPD 75: +2.4 [−1.0, +5.8] input / +0.4 [−2.5, +3.3] output on pass 1, and 0.0 [−3.4, +3.3] / +5.0 [+2.0, +8.0] on pass 2. RS-SFT 283 vs plain 400: +6.6 [+3.1, +10.1] / +5.9 [+2.8, +9.3] (pass 2: +7.1 / +5.9). OPD 75 vs plain 400: +4.3 [+0.9, +7.9] / +5.5 [+2.3, +8.8] (pass 2: +7.1 / +0.9 [−2.3, +4.0]). Against E (pass 1): RS-SFT 283 +2.0 [−1.5, +5.5] / +6.9 [+3.8, +10.1]; OPD 75 −0.4 [−3.8, +3.0] / +6.5 [+3.5, +9.5]; plain 400 −4.6 [−8.4, −1.0] / +1.0 [−2.4, +4.5]. Pass-1 and pass-2 pairings share the training runs; they are two draws of the evaluator, not two experiments.

Response shape: B leaves no final answer after the thinking block in 1,110 of 1,600 CruxEval responses; E in about 90. The same count was not made for the three arms, so part of each arm's gain may be this shape change. The 97 prompts with no execution-correct E sample among 8 (26 input, 71 output) score low for every model. Correct/n on pass 1 and pass 2: B 1/26, 1/71; E 2/26, 1/71 and 1/26, 4/71; plain 400 0/26, 3/71 and 0/26, 4/71; RS-SFT 283 4/26, 8/71 and 4/26, 9/71; OPD 75 3/26, 6/71 and 2/26, 2/71. The slice was selected by E failing all 8 samples on these prompts, so E's low score is selection-induced. RS-SFT saw no demos for these prompts. Comparing different methods on 97 selected prompts does not identify the effect of omitting them, so these are counts only.

Cost (H100-hours, Iris task-runtime accounting). Training figures are full-run costs for 4 epochs and include in-gang startup, native saves and exports; they exclude CPU preprocessing, demo generation and evals. The selected RS-SFT checkpoint is update 283 of 376 and the selected OPD checkpoint is update 75 of 100; costs are not pro-rated to the candidate. OPD's allocation-to-checkpoint figure comes from the run's log timestamps and ends at the checkpoint request, so it excludes the native save; plain SFT's 61.6 runs through its final HF export and job teardown. The two selected-cost endpoints are therefore not identical.

| Arm | Training (full 4-epoch run) | Demo generation | Exports | Allocation to selected checkpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E (expert) | 35.9 for 3 epochs (+15.3 in aborted attempts) | GLM traces via relay, no GPU-h on our side | in-gang | — |
| Plain SFT | 61.6 | shares the one k=8 E collection (14.6 measured once for all 12,800 demos, plus a 0.7 pilot; plain used 1 of the 8 samples, and no standalone 1-sample generation run was timed) | in-gang | 61.6 (final checkpoint selected) |
| RS-SFT | 57.4 | the same k=8 E collection (14.6, counted once for both SFT arms) + CPU execution grading | in-gang | full run 57.4; update 283 was not timed separately |
| OPD | 376.4 (6 nodes × 7h50m) | none (on-policy) | 58.8 (4 export-only jobs, 14–15 each) | 286.9 from allocation start to the update-75 checkpoint request (before the native save completes), plus its 14.2 export job |

OPD also spent 73.5 H100-h on smoke tests, debugging and the export path and 4.6 on a startup failure (missing W&B key) before the full run. These training-only figures are not the experiment total; the ledger adds evaluation (about 3.3 per CruxEval pass), failed-eval overhead, E and E+ training, and the reference runs. OPD per-update wall time was 4–5 min (256 sampled responses, 30,720-token cap) against about 17 s per SFT update; one prompt epoch is 4 rollouts per prompt for OPD and 1 demo for SFT, so epochs are matched on prompts, not on tokens or compute. One CruxEval pass costs about 3.3 H100-h; the ledger lists every eval run. Failed eval groups (serve preemption with a stale endpoint in the eval runner, and one preflight disconnect; see below) cost about 11 H100-h.

Confidence. The gains over B are large relative to noise (the lower 95% bound of every arm's paired gain over B is at least 9.8 pp). Between arms, the measured two-pass means put RS-SFT 1.2 / 2.7 pp above OPD and both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; each arm is one training run with no LR sweep, same-checkpoint pass pairs moved 0.5–3.1 pp on the six repeated checkpoints, and two repeats do not estimate run-to-run variance, so the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering is unresolved and the gap to plain SFT is the better-supported difference. The last-checkpoint drops in RS-SFT (input) and OPD (output) are each supported by two passes but one training run; see the selection paragraph for the statistical limits.

Deviations from the plan in the issue body.

- Plain SFT used one sample per prompt (E's sample 0, 1,600 rows), and RS-SFT used the first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows), instead of up to 4 samples per prompt. Uncovered prompts stayed in the eval denominator.
- No LR or epoch sweep was run for any arm; every arm used LR 1e-6 and 4 epochs, with per-epoch checkpoints as the only sweep.
- OPD used 4 rollouts per prompt, so its prompt epochs are not token- or compute-matched to the SFT arms.
- GSM8K and MATH500 are both reported as collapse checks (the plan named GSM8K only).

Material failures and fixes.

- Levanter could not HF-export from an S3 reference checkpoint; fixed by plumbing `hf_save_reference_code=False`.
- MarinSkyRL accepted teachers only as HF repo ids; added staging of the teacher from S3. The export-only job's config inherited the run's distillation objective, which requires a teacher the export job does not start, so the export failed at config validation; the fix drops the distillation block from the export config. Learner nodes ran out of host memory at checkpoint save with 512 GB; the full run reserved 1024 GB.
- MarinSkyRL does not convert checkpoints to HF format during training; it writes a small export request per checkpoint, and the conversion is a separate 4-node export-only job (about 14–15 H100-h each).
- The Marin eval runner keeps the serve address it first resolved. When the serve job is preempted and re-registers on another host, the eval loops on connection errors until its timeout. Two RS eval groups were lost this way and relaunched as fresh groups; no partial outputs were reused. Not fixed yet.
- Evalchemy sends no temperature or seed, so every run samples at vLLM's default. One GSM8K run failed Evalchemy's preflight request 9 s after the serve registered (server disconnected); relaunched alone, it passed.
- GPQA-D (41.9%, needs an HF token and a 28,672-token generation cap) and MMLU-Pro (44.1%) were measured on B while choosing the benchmark, as fallbacks in case CruxEval failed the teacher gate; they were not used further.

Logical demo cost: 8 samples/prompt (shared physical collection 14.7 H100-h).

## Cross-candidate pairings (selected checkpoints; pp, 95% problem-bootstrap CI conditional on completions)

| Pair | Pass 1 vs pass 1 | Pass 2 vs pass 2 |
|---|---|---|
| RS 283 vs OPD 75 | +2.4 [−1.0,+5.75] / +0.4 [−2.5,+3.25] | +0.0 [−3.4,+3.25] / +5.0 [+2.0,+8.0] |

Pass-1 and pass-2 pairings share the training runs; they are two draws of the evaluator, not two experiments.

## Pre-arm history (from the removed running-log comments; full archive in `issue-9920-comment-archive.md`)

- E run history: attempt 1 died at W&B init (no API key forwarded); attempt 2 failed at the step-91 HF export (`reference_checkpoint` pointed at a regional S3 copy; fixed by `hf_save_reference_code=False`); attempt 3 `/karan/task133-crux-sft-…/2026.10.07.5` succeeded, final loss 0.437 at step 272, 35.9 H100-h (+15.3 in the aborted attempts).
- E checkpoints, single pass: step 91 (epoch 1) 617 = 77.1 / 560 = 70.0, GSM8K 92.6, MATH500 89.0; step 182 (epoch 2) GSM8K 92.4, MATH500 91.2; step 272 (epoch 3) 635 = 79.375 / 562 = 70.25 (pass 1), selected as E by the final-checkpoint rule (similar or better than 182 on both directions).
- E+ (`/karan/task147-eplus-20261008`, E + 2 epochs at LR 1e-6, fresh optimizer): step 91 638 = 79.75 / 607 = 75.9 (single pass); step 181 two passes 1,283/1,600 = 80.19 input, 1,202/1,600 = 75.13 output; GSM8K 92.6, MATH500 90.2. Separate reference, not an arm.
- B references: MMLU-Pro 44.1% over 12,032 questions (record `…172014-…-mmlu-pro-220c`); GPQA-Diamond 41.9% (249/594 over 3 repeats, 28,672-token cap, record `20261008-084156-gate-student-rlvr-step92-gpqa28k-gpqa-diamond-9022`).
- OPD smoke (task #148): attempt 1 trained but host-OOM'd at save (512 GB); attempt 2 at 1024 GB passed the gate (finite teacher advantages, positive gradient norm, export verified with router biases = B).

## Secondary diagnostic: RS-uncovered prompts

The 97 prompts with no execution-correct E sample among 8 (26 input, 71 output) score low for every model (correct / n): B 1/26, 1/71 (record c731); E 2/26, 1/71 (pass 1, record 8a4b; the slice was selected by E failing 8 samples, so E's low score here is selection-induced); plain SFT final 0/26, 3/71 (pass 1, record 6676); OPD update 50 0/26, 2/71 (record 8529). Selected checkpoints (pass 1 / pass 2): RS 283 4/26, 8/71 and 4/26, 9/71 (covered 647/774, 609/729 and 638/774, 620/729); OPD 75 3/26, 6/71 and 2/26, 2/71; plain 400 pass 2 0/26, 4/71; E pass 2 1/26, 4/71. Under this protocol it is a difficult slice; this does not establish that it is unsolvable or that missing demos cannot hurt RS. Headline scores keep the full 1,600 denominator. Script: `experiments/tutorials/slice_cruxeval.py` (joins eval rows to CruxEval ids via the captured prompt text).

## Costs (H100-hours)

Rules: per-checkpoint costs come from allocation-to-checkpoint timestamps, not pro-rating a run total (startup/export overheads differ); teacher-demo generation is reported as shared physical cost and logical per-arm share; one prompt epoch is not matched tokens (OPD 4 samples/prompt vs SFT 1).

- E: 35.9 successful + 15.3 aborted attempts; E+ 29.9.
- GLM traces: relay (no GPU-hours on our side); E demos k=8: task `/karan/task145-e-demos-k8-20261008/inference-e07ff…/0`, 8 × H100, one attempt, 1h49m39.84s = 14.622 for all 12,800 demos, counted once across SFT+RS (a 1/8 plain share is an allocation convention, not a measured cost); pilot child 5m25.9s = 0.724. Serve children show killed/Terminated at normal collector teardown; completed parents and complete.json establish success (job counter preemptions=1 but only attempt 0 exists; not a failed collection).
- Plain SFT: 61.6 (4 GPU tasks × 8 × 1h55m26s; in-gang startup/training/saves/exports).
- RS-SFT: 57.4 (4 GPU tasks × 8 × 1h47m35s; same accounting; demo grading on CPU in an isolated container, not counted).
- OPD: smoke/debug/export 73.5 (attempt 1 27.1, attempt 2 27.2, export 19.2); full-run startup failure 4.6; full run 376.4 (6 nodes × 7h50m30s); exports 14.4 + 15.1 + 14.2 + 15.1 = 58.8. Total OPD arm (excluding evals): 513.3; full run + exports only: 435.2. Allocation-to-checkpoint (48 GPUs from task start 20:32:45 UTC 2026-10-08 to the checkpoint's export-request log line; includes the ~24 min startup before step 1 at 20:57): update 25 at 23:01:18 → 2h28m33s = 118.8; update 50 at 00:40:01 → 4h07m16s = 197.8; update 75 at 02:31:21 → 5h58m36s = 286.9; update 100 at 04:22:19 → 7h49m34s = 375.7 (job total 376.4 incl. teardown). Epoch wall times: 2h28m (incl. startup), 1h39m, 1h51m, 1h51m. Each checkpoint also needs one ~14–15 H100-h export job before evaluation.
- Evals: ~25 min × 8 per CruxEval pass ≈ 3.3 each. Evaluation overhead from infra failures: RS step-94 group …015842 (serve unreachable, GPU time not retrieved, cancelled) and RS step-375 group …030945 (serve preempted 6×, eval client held the stale endpoint; serve task 1h02m ≈ 8.3 H100-h, cancelled) and OPD step-75 group …033025 (two preempted serve attempts ≈ 0.8 H100-h).

## Material failures / tweaks

- Levanter HF export from an S3 reference checkpoint (fixed: `hf_save_reference_code=False` plumbing).
- MarinSkyRL: teachers only from HF repo ids (added S3 staging); export document kept the distillation
  objective without teachers (fixed); learner-node host OOM at checkpoint save at 512 GB (reserved 1024 GB).
- Evalchemy chat client sends no temperature/seed (all runs at vLLM default 1.0); GPQA-D needs HF token and
  a smaller generation cap (reference only).
- Eval runner keeps a stale serve address after the serve job is preempted and re-registers elsewhere (two RS eval groups lost this way; relaunched as fresh groups). Not fixed; worth an issue.

## Caveats

Test-exposed prompts (all arms train on the eval set); RS-SFT uses ground-truth execution correctness to filter demos (verifier access that plain SFT and reward-replace OPD do not have) plus 8 teacher samples per prompt; supervised-token budgets differ across arms; gains include response-shape change (B leaves no
final content in 1,110/1,600 CruxEval responses; E ~90); single-pass noise; SFT and OPD differ in
batch/update geometry (16 rows/update vs 64 prompts × 4 rollouts), optimizer implementation (Levanter vs
Megatron AdamW) and data (fixed demos vs fresh rollouts).

Applet: https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/072c90b0-281e-4692-a4bf-845874c021b1/

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖

## Weight deltas against the student

A reader asked what the weight changes behind these transfers look like. Table and method below; numbers are percentages.

| Model (vs student B) | ‖Δ‖/‖B‖ all, % | attention % | expert MLPs % | shared expert % | router % | LM head % | weights changed, % | cos(Δ, Δ_expert) all | attention | expert MLPs | LM head |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expert E (CruxEval SFT, LR 1e-5, 3 ep) | 0.036 | 0.65 | 0.047 | 0.069 | 0.17 | 0.13 | 13.7 | — | — | — | — |
| Plain SFT step 399 | 0.123 | 0.30 | 0.27 | 0.31 | 0.022 | 0.41 | 41.2 | 0.05 | 0.08 | 0.05 | 0.68 |
| RS-SFT step 282 | 0.094 | 0.24 | 0.21 | 0.25 | 0.015 | 0.34 | 34.5 | 0.06 | 0.09 | 0.07 | 0.71 |
| OPD update 75 | 0.035 | 0.12 | 0.077 | 0.12 | 0.006 | 0.060 | 20.3 | 0.08 | 0.12 | 0.12 | −0.32 |

Reading:
- Everything is a small perturbation: no checkpoint moves more than 0.13% of B's weight norm overall, and the largest component change is the expert's attention at 0.65%.
- The expert (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 1,454 rows) concentrates its change in attention, the router and the LM head and leaves the MoE expert MLPs almost untouched (0.047%, 13% of weights changed). The two SFT transfer arms (LR 1e-6, 4 epochs, 1,500–1,600 rows of the expert's text) do the opposite: they move the expert MLPs 4–6× more than the expert did and touch 35–41% of all weights. OPD moves least of the three arms (0.035% overall, comparable to the expert) and touches 20%.
- Direction: none of the arms re-creates the expert's weight change. The cosines between an arm's delta and E's delta are 0.05–0.12 in attention and the expert MLPs (random directions in this dimension give ≈0). The one shared direction is the LM head, where plain SFT and RS-SFT align with E (cosine 0.68 and 0.71) while OPD moves the LM head the opposite way (−0.32). Recovering the expert's CruxEval score therefore does not require copying its weights; three different weight changes produce it.
- RS-SFT changes the weights less than plain SFT (0.094% vs 0.123% overall) while scoring higher; it trains on fewer, verifier-correct rows.

Method: every tensor of each checkpoint was compared with the student B (open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5) in float32 after widening the bf16 exports; ‖Δ‖/‖B‖ is the relative Frobenius norm over all 67.1 B weights or over one component (attention q/k/v/o and attention gates; the 26 layers' fused MoE expert MLPs, 65.4 B weights; shared experts; router weights and biases; embeddings; LM head), 'weights changed' is the share of scalars whose bf16 value differs from B's, and cos(Δ, Δ_expert) is the cosine between the checkpoint's delta and the expert's delta over the same weights. Embeddings and norms are omitted from the table (relative change ≤ 0.01% everywhere). Caveat: the exports are bf16, so training-time changes below half a bf16 ulp of a weight are invisible; magnitudes and 'weights changed' are lower bounds, and the cosines are computed only on what survived rounding. Script `experiments/tutorials/weight_delta_stats.py` (eval worktree); per-tensor results at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/scratch/karan/mopd2/review/wdelta-<model>.json`, all summaries in `wdelta-all-summaries.json`.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
> much closer frobenius norm to the original expert update

Yes, but the direction seems almost orthogonal (0.08 here, 0.05 in  #9984 )? So it doesn't seem like it's making a "similar" update in that sense. 

The simple retained tasks we used here (GSM8K, Math500, and GPQA in #9984 ) didn't show much regression, though. Small drop in IFEval-Instruct on #9984.  SFT w/rejection sampling showed what seems like a significant improvement in GPQA-D, actually. 

If there are known typical examples of interference, we could test on that, but maybe it's fine so long as we watch retained task performance?

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Final-token preference optimization (FTPO) reduced repeated tool-call opening markers from 72/156 to 1/156 on a frozen-prefix diagnostic, a 98.6% reduction. Valid first-call syntax increased from 21/156 to 42/156. The selected checkpoint improved standalone BFCL-Parity/Pi from 30/123 to 43/123, while IFBench Loose declined from 82/300 to 78/300. These are single-sample validation results; capability preservation remains unproven.

The campaign is complete. The [selected checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-BFCL-Protocol-FTPO/tree/d761ea0a94500c2aa24aa4cd71b5a149d962e5c8) is public. The [exact benchmark](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-Tool-Protocol-Replay-v1) remains private pending clarification of redistribution rights for captured client-supplied instructions and tool descriptions. An inaccessible link for an unauthenticated reader is expected. This precaution is not a finding that the captured text is confidential or that its capture violated any terms.

## Description and hypothesis

BFCL is the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard. BFCL-Parity is this campaign's fixed 123-task panel, audited against the full task set by the [partition code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3d5906590a5e572c0ccc76b815a6fcfb2a93dea6/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/data.py); its task identities are in the private benchmark manifest. Pi is the agent harness that executes model tool calls. Harbor manages task/agent integration, and Daytona supplies task containers. DPO means direct preference optimization; SFT means supervised fine-tuning.

The preceding BFCL campaign's extended DPO run degraded Pi task success from 34/123 to 0/123 after eight updates. That observation motivated testing a much narrower training signal. This experiment asks whether changing a preference at one observed invalid token boundary can reduce a recurring tool-protocol error while retaining task capability. It does not establish the cause of the earlier DPO collapse. Related work: [BFCL closeout #10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040), [localized feedback proposal #9691](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691), and [FTPO implementation #887](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/887).

The implemented target is a second `<tool_call>` immediately after an already-opened call, allowing intervening JSON whitespace. The experiment narrowed the original closure proposal to this repeated-opener case. General closing-token repairs, short repair spans, off-top-K verified alternatives, masked-SFT comparisons, and cross-harness transfer remain follow-up work.

## Benchmark design and construction

The source BFCL revision is `6bedd7878dc5d6f3456b4d80b781eb3c2d84f262`. Its campaign partition has 3,518 training-approved task identities and a separate 123-task BFCL-Parity panel. Before failure selection, task IDs were sorted by SHA-256 of `repeated-opener-v1:<task_id>`; the first 704 were reserved for diagnostics and the other 2,814 for this intervention's training.

The builder scanned 717 of 718 retained trajectory archives and examined 5,771 records on reserved tasks. One archive was excluded for disagreement between literal opener strings and special-token positions. It excluded 857 candidate prefix occurrences over the 24,576-token limit, then selected the lexicographically smallest eligible prefix hash per task. This produced 156 unique task prefixes of 10,101–24,558 tokens. A separate training partition supplied 581 replay prefixes. No diagnostic or parity task entered this FTPO training set.

Training selection used the same source-archive set and repeated-opener extraction rule, restricted to training task IDs. It examined 22,003 training records, found 14,761 within-budget candidate occurrences, and excluded 2,880 oversized occurrences and two audited token-alignment failures. Selection kept the smallest prefix hash per task, then removed nine selected prefixes that failed the runtime boundary-selector check. The final 581 prefixes represent 581 distinct tasks. Archive overlap is expected; task identities are disjoint. See [training construction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3d5906590a5e572c0ccc76b815a6fcfb2a93dea6/experiments/post_training/skill_acquisition/training_data.py).

Each diagnostic retains exact model-input token IDs through an initial opener, immediately before a historical repeated opener at the first malformed call in an assistant span outside thinking. Historical source identity: `users/benfeuer/inputs/bfcl-rl-recovered-policy@2026.10.04.26:479563dc`. The selected prefixes contain its prior conversation and harness context. New continuations are generated from the evaluated policy. The source model is distinct from the later Recovery initializer.

The case-file SHA-256 is `9249b4a7f25d45ab6884c152cd6d975d71312e0c8ba1ecf29bf0cffaea62d8ed`. The Recovery tokenizer SHA-256 is `6a61ca2105a54e9984169b409581f31cc50330d1b47104af13c221b05e462e45`. The private dataset includes cases, construction code, manifest, exclusions, scorer, usage instructions, and aggregate/per-case diagnostic labels. Training data remains private.

This is a failure-enriched validation set repeatedly used during development and selection. It is not an untouched test or representative BFCL sample. Task-ID separation does not establish absence from the initializer's earlier training; original source records lack task-content hashes. The frozen histories were collected under an earlier harness, whereas live task evaluation uses Pi. No cross-harness learning claim follows from that combination.

## Online training protocol

All completed candidates start independently from [Grug-67B-A2B-BFCL-Recovery](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-BFCL-Recovery/tree/850a32627724d274004241dd10f6cb46fd3f6f83), the prior BFCL `.304/hf/step-1` export, with a frozen reference. The selected run is `2026.10.12.2`, export `global_step_4`; suffixes identify dated run versions, not numbers of optimizer updates.

The loop samples fresh continuations from historical training-only prefixes. At most one repeated-opener boundary per response supplies a target. The rejected token is the repeated opener. Accepted alternatives must be among the captured top-20 candidates and decode to `{` after whitespace trimming. Candidate filtering uses relative `min_p=0.01` and at most 20 accepted tokens. A legal opening brace does not prove that the remaining call will be valid. Empty-target batches skip the optimizer.

FTPO applies a selected-position logit-margin preference loss. For chosen-minus-rejected logit difference `d`, its margin-2 term is `softplus(2-d) * clamp((2-d)/2, 0, 1)`, averaged over accepted alternatives. Frozen-reference squared-logit regularization uses `lambda_mse=0.4`, targeted-token `lambda_mse_target=0.05`, and target deadband `tau_mse_target=0.5`. Token-frequency balancing strengths are 0.3 for rejected tokens and 0.5 for chosen tokens. The pinned implementation defines masking and global weighted normalization. The stronger-regularization run changes `lambda_mse` to 0.8.

No critic, learned reward model, or PPO task-reward objective is used. Fresh generation makes the continuations on-policy; the conditioning histories remain fixed historical replays. This is not full multi-turn on-policy task training. A one-token supervision target still requires model forward/backward computation and changes shared parameters.

| Setting | Executed configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Optimizer | AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, gradient clip 0.5 |
| Learning rate | Constant `4e-6`; runs `2026.10.12.3` and `.4` use `2e-6`; no warmup |
| Batch | 16 prompts, 2 continuations each, one update epoch; train/forward microbatch 2 |
| Allocation | 192 H100s: policy 120, reference 64, inference 8 |
| Parallelism | Policy pipeline 15 × expert 8; reference pipeline 8 × expert 8; TP/CP/SP 1, no packing |
| Generation | Seed 42, temperature 1, top-p 1, 8,192 new tokens; 73,728-token serving window |
| Diagnostic stop | `</tool_call>` retained in output; special tokens retained; no constrained decoding |
| Evaluation cadence | Initial, every two configured steps, and final; one-step smokes also evaluate at step 1 |
| Live task harness | Pi 0.87.0, chat-template thinking format, Daytona, 32 concurrent trials; 2 CPU/4 GiB RAM/10 GiB disk; trial timeout 1,800 seconds, verifier 300 seconds |

Raw-token protocol replay needs no container. Live BFCL/Pi task evaluation uses Daytona. Checkpoint step numbers must be distinguished from applied updates: the selected four-step run applied three updates and skipped one zero-signal batch.

The replay diagnostic uses temperature 1, top-p 1, seed 42, and an 8,192-token budget, with exactly one fresh continuation per prefix at each checkpoint. Training uses two continuations per prompt. “Single-sample” refers to one evaluated continuation per case, without repeated-generation uncertainty measurement.

Exact retained configs: https://gist.github.com/penfever/76cd73ba893caf0e1b734c625f4e22b4 and https://gist.github.com/penfever/1aae120f47647a2b34df69a62863a89e. These include source, resolved launch, and captured live-resolved files, with byte hashes and caveats about historical storage paths and attempt IDs. Runtime defaults absent from YAML are listed in the gist README and pinned source. Private data and cluster dependencies prevent a public one-command rerun.

## Results measurement

The protocol diagnostic assigns the first applicable category: repeated opener, malformed JSON, invalid generic call envelope, missing/misplaced closer, or valid first-call syntax. The envelope requires a nonempty string `name` and object-valued `arguments`. This does not check tool availability, its argument schema, execution, or later calls. The packaged scorer independently reproduced all 468 retained diagnostic labels at selected-run steps 0, 2, and 4.

| Selected run, configured step | Repeated opener | Malformed JSON | Invalid envelope | Missing/misplaced closer | Valid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 72 | 27 | 23 | 13 | 21 |
| 2 | 11 | 47 | 47 | 17 | 34 |
| 4 | 1 | 58 | 42 | 13 | 42 |

Among the 72 cases initially labeled repeated opener, final labels were 12 valid, 36 malformed JSON, 19 invalid envelope, four missing/misplaced closer, and one repeated opener. Every one of those 19 invalid envelopes lacked `arguments`. Many malformed responses still contain repeated marker-like content or `$LANG`. Reducing the first visible error does not imply a complete repair.

Standalone exported-checkpoint evaluation measures BFCL-Parity/Pi task success, MATH-500 accuracy, HumanEval+ pass@1, and IFBench loose-prompt accuracy. The full panel sizes are 123, 500, 164, and 300. Serving and evaluation configs are held constant across the baseline and final candidates except checkpoint identity. Inline BFCL trials are separate samples with explicit unscored cases; they are not substituted for standalone results.

| Model/run | BFCL-Parity/Pi | MATH-500 | HumanEval+ | IFBench Loose |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recovery baseline | 30/123 (24.39%) | 457/500 (91.4%) | 52.44% | 82/300 (27.33%) |
| `2026.10.12.1` | 44/123 (35.77%) | 466/500 (93.2%) | 73.78% | 72/300 (24.00%) |
| `2026.10.12.2`, released | 43/123 (34.96%) | 461/500 (92.2%) | 68.90% | 78/300 (26.00%) |
| `2026.10.12.3` | 32/123 (26.02%) | 464/500 (92.8%) | 69.51% | 79/300 (26.33%) |
| `2026.10.12.4` | 37/123 (30.08%) | 466/500 (93.2%) | 70.73% | 84/300 (28.00%) |

All standalone cases in this table were scored. For the released checkpoint, six MATH responses had no extractable answer and scored zero; BFCL recorded no errors. Run `.4` had two BFCL agent timeouts scored as failures and two unanswered MATH cases scored zero. Infrastructure exceptions in inline trials remain unscored and visible in the results tracker.

## Decision log and limitations

Integration attempts exposed dependency bootstrapping, microbatch, timeout, raw-token response, installed-tool wrapping, text-block grading, zero-update checkpoint, export, and invalid-argument transcript issues. Their configs and results remain in the tracker. Six completed learning candidates followed: two one-update smokes, a two-update run, the selected four-step run, a lower-rate run, and a stronger-reference-penalty run. They are not independent-seed replications.

The selected run met the campaign's 90% repeated-opener reduction target. Run `.4` reached 84.7%, with 28 valid first calls versus `.2`'s 42 and lower BFCL success, although `.4` outperformed `.2` on all three ancillary benchmarks. This motivated selecting `.2`. The two-update `.1` had the highest standalone BFCL score but only 81.7% opener reduction and the largest IFBench Loose decline among these candidates. The separate tracker gives each candidate's configured steps, applied updates, learning rate, and regularization.

IFBench Loose became the primary IF measure after trace inspection showed sensitivity to formatting and checker behavior; Strict remains a secondary measurement. This metric change occurred during the study and is not preregistered. Some strict failures reflect genuine instruction violations; others expose weak or mismatched validators. Loose does not remove all those defects. The IF follow-up preserves the original measurements and proposes an independently validated benchmark.

No repeated-generation unchanged-model control, masked-SFT arm, cross-harness transfer panel, or independently measured production tensor/logit equivalence was completed. Capability non-inferiority margins were not specified or demonstrated. Weight publication verified export bytes and all 39 weight shards; that is distinct from proving training/inference numerical equivalence. Some W&B runs report stale or crashed status despite successful Iris completion and retained final traces; the results use retained artifacts and actual-update evidence.

## Code and artifacts

Result posts: [figure and private-benchmark access](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043#issuecomment-6124431515); [complete retained-results tracker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043#issuecomment-6124432248).

- Marin [#10045](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10045) contains the campaign; stacked [#10058](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10058) contains closeout/review fixes. Both are open at publication. The selected run used Marin `3d5906590a5e572c0ccc76b815a6fcfb2a93dea6`; later code fixes must not be treated as part of that executed revision.
- MarinSkyRL merged changes: [#887 FTPO](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/887), [#970 DPO/validation](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/970), [#971 installed-agent engine integration](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/971), [#972 Daytona credentials](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/972), [#973 replay sessions](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/973), [#974 repeated-opener target](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/974), [#975 boundary selection](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/975), [#976 raw token prefixes](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/976), [#977 tool normalization](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/977), [#978 grading pin](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/978), [#979 training replay/checkpoint fixes](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/979), and [#980 grading pin](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/980).
- Harbor merged changes: [#255 native exact-token capture](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/255), [#256 correlation IDs](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/256), [#257 proxy cleanup](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/257). The configs specify executed dependency pins; these links include supporting and later closeout changes.
- Final training runtime: [MarinSkyRL `37ec019`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/37ec019b756cfd988ca8abd042cf25f24934224b). Capability evaluator: [Evalchemy `97fffeb`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/tree/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5). No new Evalchemy change is claimed for this campaign.
- Public aggregate evidence and figure: https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-Protocol-FTPO-Results/tree/a7bbbfbe05e16ee5cadbbcdd8135fbf59b40cfb7. Exact configs: https://gist.github.com/penfever/76cd73ba893caf0e1b734c625f4e22b4; integration attempts: https://gist.github.com/penfever/1aae120f47647a2b34df69a62863a89e. The benchmark link above requires access. Raw replay prefixes and training data are not included in the public artifacts.
- Follow-ups: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10060 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10061.

## Conclusion

This run supports a narrow result: a selected-position preference intervention can sharply reduce a repeated-opener signature on fixed held-out-from-this-training histories. Most responses still fail full first-call syntax, and capability preservation is unproven. The campaign closes with a public checkpoint, public measurements, and a private reproducibility dataset. Remaining experiments are tracked in the linked follow-ups; closing this issue does not assert that all original proposal criteria were met.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal, preserved for scope comparison</summary>

Design, implement, execute, and validate online feedback loops that target specific model failures at the smallest justified token or action span. Start with tool-call closure: after a complete valid payload, prefer a harness-accepted closing sequence over an observed invalid continuation. An open but still-valid prefix is not a failure.

The BFCL recovery campaign's extended DPO run fell from 34/123 successful Pi trials to 0/123 after eight updates. Whole-trajectory preferences did not preserve tool behavior. [Public analysis and artifacts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/tree/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b).

Reuse the online final-token preference optimization (FTPO) path in [MarinSkyRL #887](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/887) where appropriate. [Dr. Doom](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) demonstrated reduced repetitive tails, but its alternative-token selection does not verify tool repairs. FTPO already supplies exact-token candidates, a selected-position preference objective, frozen-reference logit regularization, and empty-window optimizer skipping. Its supported topology excludes TP>1, context parallelism, sequence parallelism, and packing.

Done when:

- Define separate failure predicates and positive-evidence requirements for closure, argument repair, repeated-error recovery, and eventual progress/finalization. Implement and validate closure first; mark the other behaviors as separate subsequent experiments rather than blending them into one reward.
- Preserve the exact conditioning tokens, harness/tool schema, model version, and verification evidence. A positive candidate must be valid under the same prefix. Admit verified candidates outside rollout top-K; support a short span when a delimiter is multi-token.
- Connect on-policy generation, target construction, actual optimizer updates, weight synchronization, and fresh generation in MarinSkyRL. Reuse existing roles/checkpointing; no critic or learned reward model is required for parser-verifiable cases.
- Run a Pi-only smoke and a bounded learning experiment on training-complement tasks. Compare local preference learning with positive-only masked SFT on the same repairs and an unchanged-model control. Record skipped versus applied updates and compute costs.
- Evaluate held-out protocol validity, accepted/executed calls, premature closure, repetition, and task solve rate before and after training. Evaluate other harnesses to measure transfer; do not infer transfer from Pi alone. Keep BFCL-Parity out of mined training targets.
- Publish pinned configuration, provenance, failure examples cleared for redistribution, and results including regressions. State that token-local supervision changes shared model weights and does not guarantee globally local effects or one-token compute cost.

[Campaign closeout #10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040); related work: [datakit local-pair mining #10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042) and [online multi-harness integration #10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041). [Detailed proposed interventions](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/dpo-repair-versus-online-rl-20261011.md).

</details>

# Research

The BFCL campaign's native DPO initializer scored 34/123 on Pi, then 0/123 after eight updates; the [closeout](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040) attributes no proven mechanism to the collapse. The pinned October code configures required trajectory retention and native DPO with recurring Pi evaluation, but its older online launcher disables inline evaluation and starts from a recovery export rather than the audited final initializer. [MarinSkyRL FTPO #887](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/887) supplies a selected-position objective for repetition; it has not verified tool-call repairs. This is an experiment and integration task, not a small isolated fix; [#10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041) owns the general online loop and [#10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042) owns offline pair mining.

**Relevant code**
- [`collect.py#L93-L175`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/collect.py#L93-L175) — Pi trace and token retention.
- [`launch.py#L68-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/launch.py#L68-L145) — older online recipe and disabled evaluation.
- [`final_dpo.py#L94-L220`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/final_dpo.py#L94-L220) — initializer, DPO, and Pi evaluation wiring.
- [`data.py#L48-L69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl/data.py#L48-L69) — audited complement/parity split.

# Localized online closure proposal

## Design

1. Define four separate predicates and evidence levels: closure after a complete valid tool payload, argument repair, repeated-error recovery, and eventual progress/finalization. Implement closure first. Mark the other three as later experiments with their own verified positives; do not pool them into a closure reward. An open, still-valid prefix and an infrastructure failure produce no target.
2. For each Pi closure target, retain the exact model-visible token prefix, generation boundary, tokenizer/model revision, tool schema, harness/runtime pins, task identity, and parser/execution receipt. Choose the shortest harness-accepted closing sequence for that *same* prefix only after a complete valid payload. Reject the observed continuation at the earliest transition that makes the call invalid. Verify the chosen sequence with the Pi parser and actual harness acceptance; parser validity alone is a weaker evidence level. Score verified candidates even when outside rollout top-K, and allow a bounded multi-token span for split delimiters. Keep BFCL-Parity identities out of targets.
3. Reuse MarinSkyRL #887's selected-position preference and frozen-reference logit regularization, extending candidate scoring and span masks only where closure requires them. Build targets from fresh Pi rollouts and connect them to non-skipped optimizer updates, weight publication, and new rollouts from the updated policy. Reuse the checkpoint/export and Pi evaluation path in `final_dpo.py`, and coordinate shared runtime work with [#10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041) and the open [TaskSession PR #9911](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9911). Keep TP=1, CP=1, sequence parallelism=1, and packing disabled until FTPO supports other topologies.
4. Run a Pi-only two-update smoke, then an at-most-eight-update pilot on the audited 3,518-task complement. Evaluate at initialization and after updates 2, 4, and 8; stop early for invalid-target admission, missing synchronization, or a marked held-out regression. Compare local preference training, positive-only masked SFT on the same verified repairs, and an unchanged initializer under matched task and evaluation conditions. Report eligible versus excluded targets, applied versus skipped updates, policy versions, GPU-hours, and any difference in training exposure.

## Validation and risks

Unit checks should reject incomplete-but-valid prefixes, changed token histories or schemas, BFCL-Parity task IDs, and unverified positives; they should cover off-top-K candidates and multi-token delimiters. The smoke must show verified targets, two applied updates, finite gradients, a saved/exported updated policy, and a fresh rollout from that policy. Held-out panels should report protocol validity, accepted and executed calls, premature closure, repetition, and task solve rate on Pi before/after training, followed by separate cross-harness panels. The control and SFT arm are needed because token-local supervision changes shared model weights; neither global locality nor one-token compute cost is implied. Publish exact pins, cleared examples, verification receipts, costs, and regressions, including a negative result if closure improves without task solves.

## Open questions for the smoke

- Does the pinned Pi parser expose a uniquely accepted closing sequence for each complete payload, including delimiters split across tokens? If several sequences pass, record all and choose a deterministic one before training.
- Does the selected MarinSkyRL runtime expose the same model-visible prefix at candidate scoring and rollout time? Any mismatch should block target admission rather than be silently retokenized.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Smartie evaluation scheduling and runtime handoff update: native validation, named sampling profiles, and inline Harbor cohorts now share one bounded, fair admission pool. Evaluation pauses new training submissions, drains submitted generation, reserves all rollout workers, and synchronizes the policy once. It then runs every selected validation row and repetition under frozen weights before training resumes. Native rows do not enter the training buffer. Cancellation or incomplete coverage fails the sweep rather than reporting partial success.

The global cap is `trajectory_runner.max_concurrent_tasks` in individual trials; training `max_in_flight` still counts multi-sample prompt groups. Harbor cohorts retain per-source caps inside this pool. A credential-isolated child runs Harbor's actual per-trial lifecycle over a control socket, including retries and artifact publication. Session summaries report worker dispatch counts, source progress, peak concurrency, and whether sources were simultaneously active. Direct, HTTP, and streaming chat paths request exact token IDs at the common inference-client boundary so replay assembly does not reconstruct IDs from decoded text.

[Scheduling contract and callback interface](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/ea93af58f92a8d31d84004b90c95265dd3333c26/docs/evaluation-scheduling.md). The branch also carries the campaign's optional mixed structural objectives, task serialization and tool-budget fixes, Daytona routing, and host-side judge credentials. The four task-runtime packages are explicitly pinned to [Marin cdb87be3](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/cdb87be31fce26ee6a078e3b207f34362d080831), which preserves these APIs on the current provider/session contracts; they require published-version adoption after those APIs land, not a claim of compatibility with the older published runtime.

The frozen CPU suite passed 2,673 tests with nine skips. Following advisory-review cleanup, 248 infrastructure/evaluation tests passed. Actual migrated inputs (69,487 training rows and 910 native validation rows) all validate against the pinned runtime. The frozen Linux runtime export and built-wheel metadata agree on the four immutable source pins. A fresh standalone wheel-resolution check could not resolve the required published Rigging version from the queried index; the validated path is the frozen source-workspace environment. The full-geometry live GPU smoke is pending, and no evaluation speedup is claimed yet.
